<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for
<br class="ltx_break">Omni AI-Generated Video Detection</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Yipeng Du<sup id="id1" class="ltx_sup">1,2,*</sup>, Yuxi Li<sup id="id2" class="ltx_sup">2,<math id="m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math></sup>, Ying Zhang<sup id="id3" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>, Chong Sun<sup id="id4" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>,
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;">
Chen Li<sup id="id5" class="ltx_sup">2,<math id="m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ddagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>‡</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ddagger</annotation></semantics></math></sup>, Jing Lyu<sup id="id6" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>, Ying Tai<sup id="id7" class="ltx_sup">1,<math id="m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ddagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>‡</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ddagger</annotation></semantics></math></sup>
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>[
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>[
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections. Even with adaptive investigation, optimizing the investigation policy alone does not directly improve the forensic capabilities of fixed experts. We introduce <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WeVisForensics</span>, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues. The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents. Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DTPO</span>, closes this loop through fast reinforcement learning of the investigator and slower refinement of the inspectors, guided by annotated artifact intervals, to report subtle artifacts they once dismissed. Furthermore, we curate <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ForenCue-30K</span>, combining role-specific forensic annotations and interaction trajectories to supervise individual inspections and their coordination, with an accompanying reinforcement-learning pool. Experiments show that WeVisForensics averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, while grounding its verdicts in localized evidence.</p>
  
</div>
<figure id="S0.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/overview.png" id="S0.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/217;" width="476" height="217" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S0.F2.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S0.F2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of WeVisForensics.<span id="S0.F2.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> <span id="S0.F2.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Top:</span> the investigator <math id="S0.F2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> repeatedly calls an inspector <math id="S0.F2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> on a temporal scope <math id="S0.F2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, reads its report <math id="S0.F2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and issues a verdict with the evidence chain. <span id="S0.F2.8.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Middle:</span> DTPO updates the investigator on every batch, while the trainable inspectors self-evolve on a slower timescale. <span id="S0.F2.8.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Bottom:</span> accuracy on the four evaluation benchmarks against representative detectors.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Rapid advances in video generation have improved the visual fidelity, temporal coherence, and realism of synthetic content, bringing new possibilities to media creation. The same progress makes fabricated recordings increasingly difficult to distinguish from authentic ones, raising concerns over misinformation, impersonation, and public trust. Reliable AI-generated video detection is therefore becoming an essential component of media forensics, where decisive cues span visual, textual, and audio dimensions and call for role-specific inspection (Figure <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To meet this need, recent studies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>, <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>, <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> use multimodal large language models (MLLMs) either to reason about authenticity in natural language or to coordinate expert analysis. However, as illustrated in Figure <a href="#A5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ Appendix E Additional Evolution Comparisons ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>, these approaches still face two challenges in how forensic evidence is examined and used. <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a) Holistic single-pass reasoning.</span> CoT-centric methods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>, <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> judge the whole video in one pass, with one model covering every artifact type. Artifacts confined to a brief interval or a small region are easily missed or explained away by hallucinated rationales (Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>a), and claims entangled in one free-form trace cannot be checked or supervised individually. <span id="S1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">b) Static workflows or coordinator-only learning.</span> Agent-based detectors either run a fixed expert pipeline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite> or train only the coordinator over fixed specialists. ARGUS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite> collects four expert reports and freezes the observers while training the judge, so irrelevant reports can outweigh the one that finds the artifact (Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>b). Tool-augmented detectors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>, <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite> instead learn when to invoke tools, yet keep tool backends fixed. Both remain bounded by the local accuracy of frozen sub-agents, since an inspector that misses a subtle cue limits what better routing or aggregation can recover (Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, right).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To overcome these challenges, we introduce <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WeVisForensics</span> (Figure <a href="#S0.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), an agentic paradigm that couples adaptive evidence collection with a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents coordinated by a main investigator agent along two complementary designs. <span id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1) Adaptive forensic analysis.</span> The Forensic Sub-agent Library (FSL) holds trainable inspectors that examine visual appearance, physical consistency, commonsense plausibility, and on-screen text, while audio tools inspect the soundtrack when one is present. Each call specifies a forensic role and a temporal scope, and the selected inspector returns findings that inform subsequent reasoning. The investigator uses these observations to request further inspections or issue an authenticity verdict, so evidence collection adapts to each video beyond a predefined workflow. <span id="S1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2) Investigator-inspector self-evolution.</span> Adaptive dispatch still relies on what each inspector can detect, so the inspectors must also improve from the calls they serve. Yet because the investigator decides which inputs the inspectors encounter while their responses shape its decisions, updating both on every batch makes each a moving target for the other. Our <span id="S1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DTPO</span> (<span id="S1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D</span>ual-<span id="S1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">T</span>imescale <span id="S1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">P</span>olicy <span id="S1.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">O</span>ptimization) therefore trains both from shared trajectories on two timescales (Figure <a href="#S2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). The investigator’s inspection policy is updated on every rollout batch using outcome rewards and call-level feedback. The inspectors accumulate the calls issued by the investigator, keep those grounded in annotated artifact intervals, select responses with interaction feedback for privileged distillation, revise their skill cards of reporting rules, and periodically refresh the FSL. The refined inspectors then return to subsequent rollouts, so the agent evolves from its own environment.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Moreover, existing forensic video datasets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite> supervise a single detector with a verdict or a holistic rationale, providing neither role-specific evidence for sub-agents nor trajectories for coordinating them. We therefore curate <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ForenCue-30K</span>, which decomposes forensic supervision by role. Each record isolates one forensic perspective and specifies a verdict, a confidence, and the temporal interval of the artifact, so that a sub-agent learns to report what its role can verify, including when the evidence is inconclusive. Agentic trajectories are assembled from executed sub-agent calls rather than imagined observations, so every decision is conditioned on evidence the main agent would actually receive. An accompanying RL pool supports DTPO. Since existing benchmarks score only the final verdict, we build <span id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AgenticCue</span>, an agentic benchmark that groups generated videos by forensic category and evaluates both detection accuracy and whether an agent invokes the relevant sub-agents.
Our contributions are threefold:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose <span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DTPO</span>, an RL algorithm in which the investigator and its inspectors co-evolve from shared interactions on fast and slow timescales. Inspectors refine their weights and skill cards on the very calls the investigator issues, so its rollouts become their curriculum.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present <span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WeVisForensics</span>, an agentic video forensics framework in which a main agent adaptively dispatches inspections to the FSL. The invocation strategy and sub-agent competence are jointly learned through DTPO.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We curate <span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ForenCue-30K</span>, a role-structured dataset with agentic trajectories covering diverse generators, and introduce <span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AgenticCue</span>, the first agentic forensic benchmark that evaluates both accuracy and call precision.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>WeVisForensics Agent Framework</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">WeVisForensics treats AI-generated video detection as an investigation rather than a single act of perception. A human forensic analyst rarely judges a video from one glance: they form a hypothesis from the overall content, zoom in on the moment and the region where it can be tested, consult the appropriate specialist, and keep collecting evidence until the conclusion is supported. WeVisForensics turns this workflow into an agent system with two levels. A main agent, the <span id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">investigator</span>, plans the investigation, and a Forensic Sub-agent Library (FSL) of <span id="S2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">inspectors</span> examines the video from complementary forensic perspectives and returns structured evidence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The framework is built on three design principles.
<span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(i) Separation of planning and perception.</span> The investigator decides <span id="S2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">what</span> to check and <span id="S2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where</span>, while each inspector decides <span id="S2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">whether</span> the artifact of its specialty is present in the requested scope. Planning thus scales with the complexity of a video, and perception remains specialized and verifiable.
<span id="S2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(ii) Role-decomposed evidence.</span> Every inspection returns a verdict, a calibrated confidence, and a visibly grounded explanation for a single forensic perspective. Each piece of evidence can therefore be audited, supervised, and credited on its own, instead of being entangled in one free-form rationale.
<span id="S2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iii) Evolvable components.</span> The parts of the system whose competence depends on the changing distribution of generators, namely the investigation policy and the visual inspectors, are trained to improve from the system’s own interactions, whereas measurement-like tools stay fixed and provide a stable reference. Sec. <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Investigation Protocol ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> specifies the investigation protocol, Sec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Forensic Sub-agent Library ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> describes each member of the FSL, and Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents the training pipeline.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/method.png" id="S2.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/185;" width="467" height="185" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S2.F3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">WeVisForensics and its training strategy, DTPO.<span id="S2.F3.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The investigator rolls out with a fixed FSL snapshot and is updated on every batch with outcome rewards and CLUE. Grounded calls (<math id="S2.F3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{OPD}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>OPD</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{OPD}}</annotation></semantics></math>) queue by role in the interaction pool, from which the slow process distills privileged EMA teachers into students, revises skill cards, and refreshes the FSL every <math id="S2.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> steps.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Investigation Protocol</h3>

<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Observation and actions.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An investigation starts from a global overview of the video: frames sampled at approximately 1 FPS across the full duration and uniformly reduced to at most 16, each tagged with its absolute timestamp, together with the duration and an indicator of whether an audio stream is present. At every turn, the investigator emits a single structured message consisting of a reasoning field and an action. The reasoning states the current hypothesis, what the evidence gathered so far does or does not establish, and why the next inspection is informative. Before the final answer, it synthesizes all returned evidence, including contrary and inconclusive findings. The action either calls one tool with its arguments, a temporal window <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[t_{s},t_{e}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[t_{s},t_{e}]</annotation></semantics></math> for the window-based inspectors, a single timestamp for OCR, and no arguments for the whole-track audio tools, or terminates the investigation with a real/fake verdict.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Formally, a video <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> with label <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\in\{\text{real},\text{fake}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext>real</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>fake</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\in\{\text{real},\text{fake}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and duration <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is first summarized by the overview</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{x}=\big(\{(f_{k},\nu_{k})\}_{k=1}^{K},\;T_{x},\;\alpha_{x}\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{x}=\big(\{(f_{k},\nu_{k})\}_{k=1}^{K},\;T_{x},\;\alpha_{x}\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the frame at absolute timestamp <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{x}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{x}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates an audio stream. Let <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the main policy and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{\phi_{s}}\}_{s\in\mathcal{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{\phi_{s}}\}_{s\in\mathcal{S}}</annotation></semantics></math> the FSL members. At turn <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the history <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}=(o_{x},a_{1},z_{1},\ldots,a_{t-1},z_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}=(o_{x},a_{1},z_{1},\ldots,a_{t-1},z_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math> contains the overview and all preceding interactions. An inspection action <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=(s_{t},u_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=(s_{t},u_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> specifies the sub-agent <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and its scope <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid h_{t}),\qquad z_{t}\sim p_{\phi_{s_{t}}}(\cdot\mid v(x,u_{t}),q_{s_{t}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid h_{t}),\qquad z_{t}\sim p_{\phi_{s_{t}}}(\cdot\mid v(x,u_{t}),q_{s_{t}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v(x,u_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(x,u_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is the input extracted from scope <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (sampled frames for visual sub-agents and the soundtrack for audio tools), <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{s_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{s_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the role instruction together with the sub-agent’s skill card (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Stage II: DTPO ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>), and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the response appended to the history. The investigation ends with an answer action <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{L}=\textsc{answer}(\hat{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">answer</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{L}=\textsc{answer}(\hat{y})</annotation></semantics></math>, producing the trajectory <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=(o_{x},a_{1},z_{1},\ldots,a_{L-1},z_{L-1},a_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=(o_{x},a_{1},z_{1},\ldots,a_{L-1},z_{L-1},a_{L})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Call budget and protocol rules.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be the number of tool calls in <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\subset\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>aud</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\subset\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> the audio tools. An inspection action <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=(s,u)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=(s,u)</annotation></semantics></math> is admissible only if</p>
<table id="S2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}&lt;4,\qquad(s,u)\notin\{a_{t^{\prime}}\}_{t^{\prime}&lt;t},\qquad u\subseteq[0,T_{x}],\qquad s\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\Rightarrow\alpha_{x}=1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∉</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>aud</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}&lt;4,\qquad(s,u)\notin\{a_{t^{\prime}}\}_{t^{\prime}&lt;t},\qquad u\subseteq[0,T_{x}],\qquad s\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\Rightarrow\alpha_{x}=1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">that is, at most four calls, no repeated call, scopes inside the video, and no audio tools on silent videos. The answer action is admissible once at least one call has succeeded, so an investigation has at most five assistant turns. A trajectory is <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">valid</span> if every message parses and every action is admissible, and it is scored as</p>
<table id="S2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R(\tau)=\mathbb{1}[\tau\text{ is valid}]\cdot\mathbb{1}[\hat{y}=y]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>τ</mi><mtext> is valid</mtext><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\tau)=\mathbb{1}[\tau\text{ is valid}]\cdot\mathbb{1}[\hat{y}=y],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so malformed messages and rule violations count as errors. Within these limits, the investigator is instructed to choose the smallest sufficient set of inspections rather than exhausting the budget: an obvious, well-localized artifact often needs one call, and a further call is justified only by an independent uncertainty or complementary evidence. Temporal scopes are kept within one continuous shot. For videos longer than 30 seconds, the investigator targets a localized event, normally within a 15-second window, instead of a near-full-video range.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">How reports are interpreted.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Inspector reports are dimensional and may conflict. Each visual report carries one of three verdicts, <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">issue</span>, <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_issue</span>, or <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inconclusive</span>, with a confidence of high, medium, or low. The investigator treats <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inconclusive</span> as moderate evidence that records a genuine limitation, never as a hidden decision in either direction, and treats <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_text</span>, tool failures, and purely descriptive audio profiles as neutral unless they contain a concrete inconsistency. A <span id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_issue</span> finding in one scope is not sufficient to establish the authenticity of the whole video, so the final verdict must integrate evidence across calls.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Forensic Sub-agent Library</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The FSL covers six forensic perspectives (Table <a href="#S2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 2.2 Forensic Sub-agent Library ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Four visual inspectors, one each for appearance, physical consistency, common sense, and on-screen text, share the main agent’s architecture but keep separate parameters, so that each can specialize without interfering with the others or with the investigation policy. Two audio tools analyze the soundtrack when one is present. Every visual inspector returns a structured report</p>
<table id="S2.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=(v,\,c,\,e),\qquad v\in\mathcal{V}_{s},\quad c\in\{\text{high},\text{medium},\text{low}\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext>high</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>medium</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>low</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=(v,\,c,\,e),\qquad v\in\mathcal{V}_{s},\quad c\in\{\text{high},\text{medium},\text{low}\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the verdict set of role <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> (Table <a href="#S2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 2.2 Forensic Sub-agent Library ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> is the confidence, and <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> is an explanation that cites timestamps inside the inspected scope.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span><span id="S2.T1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Members of the Forensic Sub-agent Library.</span> Scope is the argument chosen by the investigator. Evolving members update their LoRA adapter and skill card during DTPO, while fixed members provide a stable measurement reference.</figcaption>

<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">window</span>

<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.4.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;">✓</span></span></span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">OCR consistency</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">timestamp</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">frame + text crops</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">text_ok / text_suspicious / no_text</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;">✓</span></span></span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">Voice profile</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">whole track</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">soundtrack</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">descriptive profile</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">–</span></span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.7" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">ASR analysis</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">whole track</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">transcript + timings</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.7.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">timing anomaly / natural</span>
<span id="S2.T1.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.7.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">–</span></span>
</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></p>
</span></div>
</figure>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Window-based visual inspectors.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The appearance, physical, and commonsense inspectors receive the frames of the requested window decoded at 2 FPS, each labeled with its absolute timestamp,</p>
<table id="S2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="v\big(x,[t_{s},t_{e}]\big)=\big\{(x(\nu),\nu)\;\big|\;\nu\in[t_{s},t_{e}],\ 2\nu\in\mathbb{Z}\big\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="false" maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.447em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn> 2</mn><mi>ν</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\big(x,[t_{s},t_{e}]\big)=\big\{(x(\nu),\nu)\;\big|\;\nu\in[t_{s},t_{e}],\ 2\nu\in\mathbb{Z}\big\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x(\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is the frame at time <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math>, and follow a role-specific checklist. The <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">appearance</span> inspector checks texture stability under motion, the integrity of fine details and boundaries such as hair, fingers, teeth, and small objects, unexplained local changes in sharpness, ghosting or duplication, and the temporal and geometric consistency of lighting, shadows, and reflections. The <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">physical</span> inspector checks biological and kinematic motion, structural integrity of bodies and rigid objects, object permanence across occlusion, contact and grasping, and the dynamics of fluids and deformable materials. The <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">commonsense</span> inspector checks causality, contextual consistency of objects and roles, affordances, and event order. The investigator calls appearance and physical checks on most videos and reserves commonsense checks for overviews that suggest a specific semantic or causal anomaly, such as an animal performing a human task or an event whose outcome contradicts ordinary world knowledge.
All three inspectors share one reporting discipline. <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">issue</span> requires a concrete anomaly supported by the supplied frames, and <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_issue</span> requires the relevant content to be sufficiently observable and consistent. <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inconclusive</span> is returned when the required evidence is absent, not meaningfully exercised, or obscured by sampling, blur, occlusion, or resolution. Confidence is calibrated to the strength and coverage of the evidence: a largely static subject cannot support a high-confidence physical judgment, and one clean frame cannot support a high-confidence appearance judgment. Normal cuts, camera motion, motion blur, compression, stylization, and animation are explicitly not anomalies by themselves, which prevents the inspectors from equating post-production with generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">OCR inspector.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Video generators still struggle to render text: glyphs that start legible often fuse, break, drift, or melt as the clip proceeds, which makes on-screen text an independent and highly diagnostic forensic channel. Text, however, occupies a small fraction of the frame, and fine stroke structure is lost once the frame is resized for a vision-language model. The OCR inspector is therefore a three-stage pipeline operating on the single frame <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x(\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> at the timestamp <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> chosen by the investigator.
<span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(1) Localization.</span> PaddleOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> detects and recognizes candidate text lines <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{Det}(x(\nu))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Det</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{Det}(x(\nu))</annotation></semantics></math>, each with a normalized bounding box and detection and recognition confidences. A frame with <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}=\varnothing" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}=\varnothing</annotation></semantics></math> returns <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_text</span>.
<span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(2) Text-presence routing.</span> OCR detectors fire on textures, faces, and compression patterns. The inspector views the full frame with the candidate list, decides only whether genuine text exists, and selects informative regions <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{R}|\leq 6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{R}|\leq 6</annotation></semantics></math>, including subtitles, signs, labels, license plates, UI elements, and text on background objects. If every candidate is a false positive, <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}=\varnothing" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}=\varnothing</annotation></semantics></math> and it returns <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_text</span>.
<span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3) Crop-level glyph inspection.</span> Each region <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{i}\in\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{i}\in\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math> is cropped with a 15% margin at a higher pixel budget than the full frame. The inspector judges every crop independently against the full-frame context, assigning a crop label <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g_{i}\in\mathcal{Q}=\{" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}\in\mathcal{Q}=\{</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">regular</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">warped</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">generation-degraded</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">too blurry</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">stylized or logo</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">inconclusive<math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\}</annotation></semantics></math></span>, and looks for fused or broken strokes, malformed character topology, inconsistent repeated characters, and drifting baselines. Given its proposed verdict <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{v}</annotation></semantics></math>, the reported verdict is</p>
<table id="S2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v=\begin{cases}\texttt{inconclusive},&amp;\hat{v}=\texttt{text\_suspicious}\ \text{and}\ g_{i}\notin\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{gen}}\ \forall\,b_{i}\in\mathcal{R},\\
\hat{v},&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">inconclusive</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">text_suspicious</mtext><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∉</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mi>gen</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v=\begin{cases}\texttt{inconclusive},&amp;\hat{v}=\texttt{text\_suspicious}\ \text{and}\ g_{i}\notin\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{gen}}\ \forall\,b_{i}\in\mathcal{R},\\
\hat{v},&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{gen}}=\{" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mi>gen</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{gen}}=\{</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">warped</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">generation-degraded<math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\}</annotation></semantics></math></span>. A text-level forgery claim thus always rests on at least one crop with visibly generated glyphs.
The investigator calls OCR whenever the overview contains captions, signage, packaging, handwriting, or other text, and targets the timestamp where the text looks least stable. Figure <a href="#A6.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Appendix F Additional Inspection Examples ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Additional Inspection Examples ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> shows a complete example, in which an appearance check first flags an unnaturally smooth facial surface and a targeted OCR call then confirms malformed glyphs on the enlarged crops.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Audio tools.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Generated videos increasingly carry synthesized speech, and an inconsistency between what is heard and what is seen is often more conspicuous than any visual artifact. The <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">voice profile</span> tool performs speaker diarization, separates overlapping speech, and estimates for each speaker an age, female/male/child probabilities, and arousal, dominance, and valence scores. The report is descriptive by design: a strong age or gender conflict with a clearly visible speaking face is useful supporting evidence, whereas dubbing, voice-over, and multiple speakers must be discounted. The <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ASR analysis</span> tool transcribes the soundtrack with word-level timestamps and asks a frozen language model to review only concrete transcript and timing anomalies, such as robotic, uniformly spaced segments, against natural patterns such as hesitations and breathing pauses. Both tools are invoked on videos with an audio stream, typically when a speaking face or a talking-head scene is visible.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trainable and fixed members.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The FSL splits into <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{evo}}\cup\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{fix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>evo</mi></msub><mo>∪</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>fix</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{evo}}\cup\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{fix}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{evo}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>evo</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{evo}}</annotation></semantics></math> contains the four visual inspectors and <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{fix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>fix</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{fix}}</annotation></semantics></math> the two audio tools. Each member <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{evo}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>evo</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{evo}}</annotation></semantics></math> evolves during training through two complementary channels: its LoRA adapter <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is distilled from the investigator’s own calls, and its skill card, a short list of <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Report</span> and <span id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Ignore</span> rules appended to the role instruction <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, is revised by a reflector model (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Stage II: DTPO ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>). Visual artifacts are the cues that shift most rapidly as generators improve, and the calls issued by the investigator expose exactly the inputs, scopes, and difficulty levels on which the inspectors are consulted. The audio tools and the PaddleOCR detector remain fixed: their outputs are measurements, such as speaker attributes, transcripts, and text boxes, whose meaning should not drift while the investigator learns to interpret them, and the scarcity of labeled audio forgeries would make their adaptation unreliable. The investigator itself is optimized with reinforcement learning, so the system improves both in what it asks and in what it is told.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Data Construction</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Built from 30,000 curated videos, <span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ForenCue-30K</span> provides multi-level supervision for our framework, comprising 117,552 role-specific records for the sub-agents, 33,896 interaction trajectories for the main agent, and a 7,500-row RL pool for DTPO (Figure <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Evidence annotation. ‣ 3.1 Role-Grounded Supervision Construction ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Its construction follows three principles: <span id="S3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">broad generator coverage</span>, <span id="S3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">a role-aligned forensic taxonomy</span>, and <span id="S3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">temporally grounded evidence annotation</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Generated videos are primarily curated from public datasets (GenBuster-200K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>, RewardData <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, VBench-2.0 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>]</cite>, and AIGVDBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>) covering open-source and earlier-generation commercial models, supplemented with videos generated through AI video-generation platforms and specialized forgery domains including digital humans and speaker-mismatched audio forgeries. The generated training videos include CogVideoX <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>]</cite>, HunyuanVideo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>, LTX-Video <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, EasyAnimate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, Wan 2.1/2.2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>, Gen-2/3, Pika 1.5, Kling 1.0/1.5, MiniMax-Video-01, Veo 3, and Vidu Q1. Real videos are sourced from OpenVid-1M <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> and Koala-36M <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>, supplemented with videos collected from the stock media platforms Pexels and Pixabay.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/dataset.png" id="S3.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/197;" width="467" height="197" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S3.F4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of ForenCue-30K.<span id="S3.F4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Curated videos are annotated with role-specific artifact evidence and converted into sub-agent records and interaction trajectories, and an RL pool supports DTPO. Examples show artifacts targeted by each sub-agent.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Role-Grounded Supervision Construction</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Supervision is constructed in a pipeline that mirrors the structure of the agent (Figure <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Each curated video is first annotated separately for every forensic role, the annotations are then converted into training records for the inspectors, and executed inspector calls are finally assembled into investigation trajectories for the investigator. Every stage keeps the same role taxonomy, so the evidence an inspector learns to report is exactly the evidence the investigator learns to request and interpret.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Role-structured taxonomy.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Instead of one holistic rationale per video, supervision is organized by forensic perspective and subdivided into fine-grained artifact dimensions. Matching the six FSL roles, we categorize artifacts into <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Visual appearance</span> (26,378 records), <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Physical consistency</span> (32,348), <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Common sense</span> (40,246), <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">OCR consistency</span> (18,580), <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ASR analysis</span>, and <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Audio profile</span>. Visual appearance covers texture and detail integrity, boundary blending, ghosting, and the consistency of lighting, shadows, and reflections. Physical consistency covers body and object structure, kinematics, object permanence, contact, and fluid or deformable dynamics. Common sense covers causality, affordances, contextual roles, and event order, and OCR consistency covers glyph structure and the temporal stability of rendered text. The audio roles cover the plausibility of speech timing and the agreement between the voice and the visible speaker. Each record isolates one perspective and specifies a verdict (issue, no-issue, or inconclusive), a confidence, an explanation, and the temporal interval of the artifact. Real videos contribute records under the same format, so every role sees both outcomes. This balance teaches each inspector to report only what its role can verify, rather than to equate “generated” with “an artifact of my type is visible”.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evidence annotation.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each video and role, a rubric-conditioned VLM annotator examines the timestamped frames under a role-specific guideline listing the artifact dimensions above and source-provenance constraints, localizing observable artifacts within temporal intervals and writing frame-grounded explanations of what is visibly wrong. Explanations must refer strictly to observable visual evidence, and roles without visible anomalies are recorded as no-issue even on generated videos, preventing forced attribution. A cross-family VLM verifier then checks each candidate against the video and refines or rejects it, filtering hallucinated explanations, over-generalized commonsense claims, and imprecise intervals. Human reviewers inspect sampled annotations per source and role during prompt development and source onboarding, and their findings are fed back into the guidelines and filtering rules, while audio inconsistencies are annotated directly by reviewers who watch each clip with sound (Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>). In a quantitative audit of 340 video–role annotations, <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> are supported by the visual evidence.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span><span id="S3.T2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with existing forensic video training data.</span> Role: per-perspective records.
