<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">FaceVid-Forensics-100K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;">✓</span></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;">✓</span></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B30000;">✗</span></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B30000;">✗</span></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B30000;">✗</span></span>

<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;--ltx-bg-color:#E0E0E0;">✓</span></span>

<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;--ltx-bg-color:#E0E0E0;">✓</span></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;--ltx-bg-color:#E0E0E0;">✓</span></span>
<span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S3.T2.7.1.1.1.1.1.1.6.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#009900;--ltx-bg-color:#E0E0E0;">✓</span></span>

</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></p>
</span></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inspector records.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each annotation is converted into a record whose input is exactly what the inspector observes at inference: the frames of the requested window at 2 FPS for the window-based roles, and the frame at the requested timestamp for OCR. The target is the structured report, comprising the verdict, the confidence, and an explanation that cites timestamps within the window. Because the windows are specified in absolute video time, the same annotation can supervise the inspector and later serve as the grounding interval <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{x,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{x,s}</annotation></semantics></math> for selecting calls during DTPO.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trajectory synthesis.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Interaction trajectories are constructed through execution-grounded synthesis. Given the video overview and verified role evidence as training-only context, a VLM trajectory planner decides which roles and temporal scopes to consult, modeling how an expert investigation prioritizes relevant checks. Every planned call is then executed by the corresponding inspector, and the planner writes the reasoning of each turn conditioned on the reports actually returned, so that the investigator never learns from imagined observations. All training-only metadata are stripped from student-facing messages, conditioning each decision strictly on inference-time observations. Trajectories cover both real and generated videos, use about two calls on average under the four-call budget, and reach <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> appropriate tool selection in a human audit of 100 trajectories.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RL pool.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The name ForenCue-30K refers to the core video supervision set, while expanded annotation records, trajectories, and the accompanying RL pool are counted separately (Figure <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). The RL pool contains 7,500 rows spanning 15 collections and 56 source subsets, with 3,750 unique real and 3,180 unique generated clips repeated with source-dependent weights to balance labels and sources. Each generated clip carries its role-specific artifact intervals, which ground the selection of inspector calls in the slow process, and each clip carries a verified set of relevant roles, which defines the tool-coverage reward (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Stage II: DTPO ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Quality control.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Export checks validate record structure, role-specific fields, video duration, and the availability of sampled frames. For interaction trajectories, construction checks match call identifiers to stored responses and enforce the action budget and the protocol rules of Sec. <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Investigation Protocol ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>, and automated text checks screen the student-facing messages for training-only metadata leakage. Each trajectory record retains the video and source identifiers, sampled-frame timestamps, ordered messages, and target verdict.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>AgenticCue Benchmark</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Existing benchmarks score only the final verdict, so an agent that reaches the right answer through irrelevant inspections, or that cannot handle a particular class of artifacts, remains invisible. AgenticCue is designed to expose both. Unlike the training set, which is dominated by open-source and earlier commercial models, it targets newer-generation commercial releases (Veo 3.1, Kling 2.5/3.0, Seedance 1.5/2.0, Hailuo 2.3/H3, Wan 2.6, Sora 2, Jimeng, and HappyHorse 1.0) alongside held-out digital-human, face-swap, and voice-mismatch audio forgeries, and thus also measures generalization to generators unseen during training.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Category construction.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The benchmark spans five forensic categories, <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Visual</span>, <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Physical</span>, <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">OCR</span>, <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Common sense</span>, and <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Audio</span>, each containing exactly 500 generated videos verified to exhibit that category’s artifact. Candidate clips are first annotated by model annotators and then confirmed by human reviewers. A clip may belong to several categories, and 170 clips do, giving 2,330 unique generated videos. All categories share the same 500 real videos, so each category forms a balanced set of 1,000 videos. None of its videos appear in ForenCue-30K.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Metrics.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each category, we report binary detection accuracy on its balanced set, counting invalid or missing outputs as errors. To evaluate whether the agent consults the right specialist, we additionally report invocation precision, the fraction of generated videos on which the agent invokes tool <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> that actually call for role <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. The reference set of relevant roles for the four visual tools comes from dense annotations in which two cross-family VLM annotators independently mark every role worth inspecting on each generated video and a label-blind judge resolves disagreements, while for audio it is the Audio category. Table <a href="#S3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Metrics. ‣ 3.2 AgenticCue Benchmark ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> lists the resulting label counts and the base rates obtained by invoking a tool on every video. Precision is always read together with accuracy, which would drop if the agent skipped relevant inspections. Details are given in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Implementation Details ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span><span id="S3.T3.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Label counts behind sub-agent invocation precision (Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Evaluation on AgenticCue. ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</span> Eligible counts the generated videos scored for each role, <math id="S3.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|G_{s}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|G_{s}|</annotation></semantics></math> the videos that call for role <math id="S3.T3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, and Base the precision of invoking tool <math id="S3.T3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> on every eligible video, which is also the precision of the fixed-workflow ARGUS on its two observer roles.</figcaption>

<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Training Pipeline</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">WeVisForensics is trained in two stages. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on ForenCue-30K first teaches the investigator the investigation protocol and each inspector its role-specific reporting format (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Stage I: Supervised Initialization ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>). DTPO then lets the investigator and the inspectors improve together from their own interactions (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Stage II: DTPO ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>), and a scalable implementation keeps the joint training practical (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Scalable Implementation ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>). Every model is adapted with low-rank adapters on a shared backbone, so that the investigator and all inspectors can be loaded and served as one backbone plus a few lightweight adapters, and both stages update every model in the same parameterization.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Stage I: Supervised Initialization</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All models share the Qwen3.5-4B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> backbone. The investigator and the four visual inspectors are trained as five separate rank-64 LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> adapters (<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}128</annotation></semantics></math>) on all linear layers of the language model, and the backbone, the vision encoder, and the vision-language projector are frozen throughout, so that adaptation concentrates on forensic reasoning rather than low-level visual features.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each model is trained with the standard masked next-token objective. A training sample is a token sequence <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{L_{y}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{L_{y}})</annotation></semantics></math> with a loss mask <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{y,j}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{y,j}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> that equals one on model-authored tokens and zero on instructions, overview frames, inspector reports, tool outputs, and padding. For a model with parameters <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math> trained on a dataset <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\psi;\mathcal{D})=-\frac{\sum_{y\in\mathcal{D}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{y}}m_{y,j}\log p_{\psi}(y_{j}\mid y_{&lt;j})}{\sum_{y\in\mathcal{D}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{y}}m_{y,j}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>SFT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></msubsup><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\psi;\mathcal{D})=-\frac{\sum_{y\in\mathcal{D}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{y}}m_{y,j}\log p_{\psi}(y_{j}\mid y_{&lt;j})}{\sum_{y\in\mathcal{D}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{y}}m_{y,j}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">so the loss averages the negative log-likelihood over all supervised tokens. The investigator minimizes <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\theta;\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{inv}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>SFT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>inv</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\theta;\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{inv}})</annotation></semantics></math> on interaction trajectories, where the mask covers the reasoning, every action, and the final verdict, and each inspector <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> minimizes <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\phi_{s};\mathcal{D}_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>SFT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\phi_{s};\mathcal{D}_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> on its role-specific records, where the mask covers the structured report of Eq. (<a href="#S2.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 2.2 Forensic Sub-agent Library ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Investigator.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The investigator is trained on the 33,896 agentic trajectories of ForenCue-30K, extended with trajectories on additional videos covering a broader range of content. Each trajectory contains every executed call and returned report together with the reasoning that motivates each step and the final verdict, and is packed into one multi-turn sample with a maximum length of 32,768 tokens. The adapter is trained with a learning rate of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{\times}10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{\times}10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> and a cosine schedule with 5% warm-up in two consecutive single-epoch stages with different data orderings, and the stage-1 adapter is merged into the backbone before stage 2 begins.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inspectors.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each visual inspector is trained on its own portion of the 117,552 role-specific records, extended with records on additional videos. Each record pairs a scoped input with a verdict, a confidence, and an evidence-grounded explanation. Real and generated videos are kept in every role, so that an inspector does not learn to report an issue by default. The inspectors follow the same adapter recipe as the investigator, with a maximum length of 32,768 tokens (16,384 for OCR, whose input is a single frame). The resulting system consists of a single backbone plus five small adapters, which makes it easy to store and serve.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Stage II: DTPO</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DTPO makes interaction experience the link between learning to request evidence and refining the inspectors that provide it. The investigator determines which inputs the inspectors encounter, and the resulting reports influence both its subsequent decisions and which interactions are selected for inspector training. Updating both at the same time would make each a moving target for the other. The fast process therefore updates only the investigator on every rollout batch, while the slow process accumulates role-specific interaction queues over multiple batches and aligns the inspectors with a slowly changing EMA teacher <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>. The updated FSL then supplies observations for later rollouts, closing the loop. Video-level labels and artifact annotations are used only during training. At inference, the learned investigator and inspectors execute the protocol of Sec. <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Investigation Protocol ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> with fixed parameters.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fast process: investigator policy learning.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each input, we collect <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> interaction trajectories <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\tau_{g}\}_{g=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\tau_{g}\}_{g=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> with the current main policy and a fixed FSL snapshot. Each trajectory receives the correctness reward <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{g}=R(\tau_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{g}=R(\tau_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> of Eq. (<a href="#S2.E4" title="Equation 4 ‣ Call budget and protocol rules. ‣ 2.1 Investigation Protocol ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), so invalid trajectories receive zero. We use GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite> to normalize rewards within the group,</p>
<table id="S4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{g}=\frac{R_{g}-\overline{R}}{\operatorname{std}(R_{1},\ldots,R_{G})+\delta}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>std</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{g}=\frac{R_{g}-\overline{R}}{\operatorname{std}(R_{1},\ldots,R_{G})+\delta},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> stabilizes normalization. The terminal reward says whether the investigation succeeded, but not which of its inspections contributed. We therefore augment it with <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CLUE</span> (<span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">C</span>all-<span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">L</span>evel <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">U</span>tility <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">E</span>stimation), a per-action credit signal that measures the change in a frozen reference model’s support for the correct label after each inspection call. The reference scores the known label <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> before and after the response to call <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>. With probabilities normalized over the real/fake alternatives, let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{j}^{\mp}=\log p_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid h_{j}^{\mp})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>∓</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>∓</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{j}^{\mp}=\log p_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid h_{j}^{\mp})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{j}^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{j}^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{j}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{j}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> are the histories before and after the response. The CLUE score is</p>
<table id="S4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{j}=\operatorname{clip}\!\left(\log\frac{-\ell_{j}^{-}+\epsilon}{-\ell_{j}^{+}+\epsilon},-b,b\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.428em;" width="1.428em"><mi>clip</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{j}=\operatorname{clip}\!\left(\log\frac{-\ell_{j}^{-}+\epsilon}{-\ell_{j}^{+}+\epsilon},-b,b\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> smooths the ratio and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> bounds the score. A positive score means that the returned report moved the reference toward the correct label, and a negative score means that it misled the reference. Because the reference is distinct from both the investigator and the inspector teachers, the score measures the informativeness of the evidence itself rather than the policy’s own belief. We center scores within each GRPO group. Writing <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{g,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{g,j}</annotation></semantics></math> for the score of call <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> in trajectory <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{c}_{g,j}=c_{g,j}-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}_{j}|}\sum_{g^{\prime}\in\mathcal{G}_{j}}c_{g^{\prime},j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{c}_{g,j}=c_{g,j}-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}_{j}|}\sum_{g^{\prime}\in\mathcal{G}_{j}}c_{g^{\prime},j}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of rollouts in the group that issue at least <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> calls. The token advantages become</p>
<table id="S4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{A}_{g,t}=\begin{cases}A_{g}+\lambda\tilde{c}_{g,j},&amp;t\in\mathcal{I}_{g,j},\\
A_{g},&amp;t\in\mathcal{M}_{g}\setminus\mathcal{I}_{g},\\
0,&amp;t\notin\mathcal{M}_{g},\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∖</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{A}_{g,t}=\begin{cases}A_{g}+\lambda\tilde{c}_{g,j},&amp;t\in\mathcal{I}_{g,j},\\
A_{g},&amp;t\in\mathcal{M}_{g}\setminus\mathcal{I}_{g},\\
0,&amp;t\notin\mathcal{M}_{g},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> contains main-agent output tokens, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{g,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{g,j}</annotation></semantics></math> is the token span of inspection action <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{g}=\bigcup_{j}\mathcal{I}_{g,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>⋃</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{g}=\bigcup_{j}\mathcal{I}_{g,j}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> weights call feedback. A clipped policy-ratio objective uses <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{A}_{g,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{A}_{g,t}</annotation></semantics></math> to update the investigator. Final-answer tokens retain <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, and inspector observations and padding are masked from the loss. Inspection choices thus receive feedback on the evidence they produced, while the final decision remains trained by its outcome.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Tool-coverage reward.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Correctness alone tolerates investigations that reach the right verdict through an irrelevant inspection, and such shortcuts generalize poorly to videos whose decisive artifact lies elsewhere. Each training video therefore carries a verified set of relevant forensic roles, derived from its role-specific annotations, and each trajectory receives the F1 score between this set and the set of tools it actually invoked. The F1 score is centered within the GRPO group and added to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> with weight <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math> after the correctness normalization, so it ranks investigations that share the same outcome without overriding correctness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Slow process: collecting interactions for refinement.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Every call to a trainable inspector during rollouts is a candidate refinement example, so the main policy determines which inputs, temporal scopes, and difficulty levels the inspectors are refined on. Candidates are first grounded in annotations. Let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{x,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{x,s}</annotation></semantics></math> be the annotated artifact intervals of role <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> on a generated video <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, or the whole video if <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is real, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> the scope inspected by call <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>. The calls kept for refinement are</p>
<table id="S4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{OPD}}=\biguplus_{x}\biguplus_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\big\{\,j_{x,s}\mid u_{j}\cap I_{x,s}\neq\varnothing\,\big\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>OPD</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">⨄</mo><mi>x</mi></munder><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">⨄</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>j</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{OPD}}=\biguplus_{x}\biguplus_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\big\{\,j_{x,s}\mid u_{j}\cap I_{x,s}\neq\varnothing\,\big\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Calls on generated videos without an overlapping annotation are excluded, since failing to find an artifact in such a scope is not an error of that role. We then partition each kept response by its verdict and the video label. On a real video, a reported issue is a <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">false alarm</span> and a no-issue verdict is <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">correct</span>. On a generated video, a call that reports no issue is a <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">miss</span> and one that reports an issue is a <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">hit</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A correct verdict can still hinder subsequent forensic reasoning, for example an inconclusive or low-confidence report that leaves the investigator without usable evidence. The CLUE score in Eq. (<a href="#S4.E10" title="Equation 10 ‣ Fast process: investigator policy learning. ‣ 4.2 Stage II: DTPO ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>) identifies such responses: a correct response is relabeled as a <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">hedge</span> when <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{j}&lt;\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{j}&lt;\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> and its verdict is inconclusive or not stated with high confidence. False alarms, misses, and hedges are the responses whose decisions must change, while the remaining correct responses are retained so that refinement preserves decisions that are already right. The final trajectory need not be incorrect: a locally unhelpful report warrants refinement even when the investigator recovers the correct answer. All retained calls, rather than one call per prompt and role, enter role-specific queues. When a role is refreshed, its examples are arranged into batches with equal numbers of real and generated videos by subsampling the majority label.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Privileged inspector distillation.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Each example supplies its inspector input <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, collected response <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and privileged context <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. For role <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, an exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher receives <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, following the training-only supervision principle of privileged-information distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>, while the student retains its inference-time input. For a real video, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> states the label. For a generated video, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> lists the annotated intervals that overlap the inspected scope within the role’s specialty and instructs the teacher to locate the corresponding anomaly in the supplied frames, treating the pointer as a cue for where to look rather than as evidence. As in on-policy distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, teacher and student distributions at a collected response prefix are</p>
<table id="S4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E13.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p^{T}_{i,t}=p_{\bar{\phi}_{s}}(\cdot\mid u_{i},g_{i},z_{i,&lt;t}),\quad p^{S}_{i,t}=p_{\phi_{s}}(\cdot\mid u_{i},z_{i,&lt;t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{T}_{i,t}=p_{\bar{\phi}_{s}}(\cdot\mid u_{i},g_{i},z_{i,&lt;t}),\quad p^{S}_{i,t}=p_{\phi_{s}}(\cdot\mid u_{i},z_{i,&lt;t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> be the position where the response commits to its verdict, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> the label-consistent verdict token (issue or text-suspicious for generated videos, no-issue or text-ok for real ones), and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{v}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{v}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> its opposite. The per-role objective is</p>
<table id="S4.E14" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S4.E14X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E14X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{s}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\Big[" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo></mstyle><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></msup><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{s}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\Big[</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E14X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{\sum_{t=1}^{|z_{i}|}w_{i,t}\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(\operatorname{sg}[p^{T}_{i,t}]\,\|\,p^{S}_{i,t}\right)}{\sum_{t=1}^{|z_{i}|}w_{i,t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msup><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mi>D</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>KL</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>sg</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>S</mi></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{\sum_{t=1}^{|z_{i}|}w_{i,t}\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(\operatorname{sg}[p^{T}_{i,t}]\,\|\,p^{S}_{i,t}\right)}{\sum_{t=1}^{|z_{i}|}w_{i,t}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.E14Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E14Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle-\beta\log\frac{e^{o_{i}(v_{i}^{\star})}}{e^{o_{i}(v_{i}^{\star})}+e^{o_{i}(\bar{v}_{i})}}\Big]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><mi>log</mi><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle-\beta\log\frac{e^{o_{i}(v_{i}^{\star})}}{e^{o_{i}(v_{i}^{\star})}+e^{o_{i}(\bar{v}_{i})}}\Big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{sg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>sg</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{sg}</annotation></semantics></math> stops teacher gradients, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{i,t}=\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i,t}=\omega</annotation></semantics></math> at decision-field tokens and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> elsewhere, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{i}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{i}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes student logits at <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> weights the label correction of the verdict. The correction contrasts only the two opposing verdicts, so it corrects the decision without suppressing the inconclusive option or other vocabulary entries. For OCR, the same objective is further grounded on double-checked <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">text-ok</span> regions drawn from generated videos, so the inspector learns that regular text on a forged clip is not itself evidence of forgery. For responses whose decisions must change, the distillation term is dropped when the privileged teacher still assigns its highest probability at <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> to the student’s original verdict, in which case only the label correction is applied. The teacher supplies token distributions at the student’s collected prefixes, so no replacement trajectory has to be generated. The teacher tracks the student via <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}_{s}\leftarrow(1-\rho)\bar{\phi}_{s}+\rho\phi_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}_{s}\leftarrow(1-\rho)\bar{\phi}_{s}+\rho\phi_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the student learning rate decays linearly over the investigator’s schedule, so the FSL settles as the inspection policy converges.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Skill-card evolution.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Adapter updates change how an inspector perceives. Some failure modes, however, are better expressed as explicit reporting rules, for example that motion blur on fast-moving hands is not a structural defect, or that a soft object deforming under direct contact is not a physics violation. Alongside its adapter weights, each trainable inspector therefore carries a skill card <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, a short list of <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Report</span> and <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Ignore</span> rules appended to its role instruction and seen by student and teacher. After each distillation round, a frozen reflector LLM reviews recent calls that the current inspector still judges wrongly, with their labels, and proposes rule edits. A candidate card replaces the current one only if it yields more correct verdicts on held-out recent calls without losing any correct verdict on either real or generated videos. This acceptance test makes card edits monotone on recent experience and prevents the reflector from trading false alarms for misses. Examples of evolved cards are given in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Learned Skill Cards ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Synchronizing fast and slow updates.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training alternates rollout collection, investigator optimization, interaction selection, and periodic FSL refinement. Each batch is collected with the current main policy and a fixed inspector snapshot. After the investigator update, selected interactions enter role-specific queues. Every <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> investigator steps, a synchronization barrier checks whether each queue contains enough examples to update its inspector. Eligible students are distilled, their skill cards are revised, and the new FSL snapshot is published before rollout collection resumes, while roles with insufficient examples retain their current parameters and keep their queues for the next barrier. This schedule lets the investigator learn between FSL updates while each refinement stage draws on accumulated interaction experience.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Scalable Implementation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A single DTPO step runs <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32\times G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\times G</annotation></semantics></math> multi-turn investigations, each invoking up to four inspectors on video inputs, so inspector serving and FSL refreshes dominate the cost of training. The investigator and the four visual inspectors are served by separate vLLM engines that share the training cluster, and the rollout workers execute investigations asynchronously, so that a slow audio or OCR call does not stall other trajectories in the batch. The audio tools and PaddleOCR run as independent services. At each synchronization barrier, the four inspector refreshes are packed into two parallel lanes of GPUs, one handling visual appearance followed by common sense and the other physical consistency followed by OCR, which balances the per-lane workload because the roles accumulate very different numbers of calls. Refreshed adapters are merged into the backbone weights and published to the inference engines as full checkpoints rather than hot-swapped as LoRA modules, which we found to be numerically more robust on our hardware. Skill-card revision runs after publication. With a refresh every 20 steps, the full joint schedule of a few hundred investigator steps completes in about a day on our cluster.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Implementation Details</h3>

<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Main models.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The base Qwen3.5-4B serves as the frozen CLUE reference <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math>. DTPO starts from the SFT adapters of Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Stage I: Supervised Initialization ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and keeps every model in the adapter parameterization. The fast process runs GRPO with <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G{=}4</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts per video, a batch of 32 videos, and at most 4 inspector calls per trajectory for one epoch over the RL pool. The investigator adapter is trained with a learning rate that warms up linearly to <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> over the first 60 steps. CLUE uses <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon{=}0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon{=}0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda{=}0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda{=}0.2</annotation></semantics></math>, the tool-coverage bonus has weight <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, and the hedge threshold is <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa{=}{-}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa{=}{-}0.05</annotation></semantics></math>. In the slow process, each visual inspector adapter is trained every <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H{=}20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H{=}20</annotation></semantics></math> investigator steps on class-balanced batches of 32 grounded calls, with a learning rate decayed linearly from <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> over training progress, <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho{=}0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho{=}0.001</annotation></semantics></math>. The RL pool used here extends the pool of Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> with additional labeled videos.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Evaluation Setup</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation protocols.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GenBuster-Bench (GB) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> serves as the in-domain benchmark. Out-of-domain evaluation uses the video track of GenBuster-Bench++ (GB++) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> and the General split of MintVid <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>. We report binary detection accuracy for GB, GB++, each of the six generator categories of MintVid General, and the five AgenticCue categories. SoTA binary detectors are trained on our dataset using their original settings.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implementation details.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The main agent and sub-agents share one Qwen3.5-4B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> backbone, and each carries its own rank-64 LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> adapter on all linear layers of the language model, initialized from its SFT adapter. The fast process runs GRPO with <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G{=}4</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts per video, a batch of 32 videos, and at most 4 sub-agent calls per trajectory for one epoch over the RL pool. The main-agent learning rate warms up linearly to <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> over the first 60 steps. In the slow process, each sub-agent adapter is trained on class-balanced batches of 32 selected interactions with an EMA rate <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho{=}0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho{=}0.001</annotation></semantics></math>. The served adapters are refreshed every 20 steps, and the sub-agent learning rate decays linearly from <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> over training progress.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Main Results</h3>

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation on standard benchmarks.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Evaluation on standard benchmarks. ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows that WeVisForensics attains the strongest detection performance on both the in-domain and the out-of-domain benchmarks. On the in-domain split, binary detectors stay near chance, whereas MLLM-based detectors benefit from domain supervision, and WeVisForensics reaches 97.7%, surpassing VideoVeritas by 3.4% and ARGUS by 11.3%. On the out-of-domain splits, generic MLLMs suffer from low fake recall regardless of scale, and CoT detectors drop sharply across unseen generators. WeVisForensics ranks first on GenBuster++ at 97.5% and on the six-generator MintVid mean at 88.0%, improving over the SFT agent on every generator category, which demonstrates strong generalization to unseen generators.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span><span id="S5.T4.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Performance comparison on AI-generated video detection.</span> MintVid General is split into six generator categories under the official repeated-reference protocol. Each Agentic category pairs 500 generated videos with 500 real videos. Avg. averages GenBuster, GenBuster++, the MintVid mean, and the Agentic mean. Best and second-best results are bold and underlined.</figcaption>

</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation on AgenticCue.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The five categories of AgenticCue expose the blind spots of prior paradigms across artifact types. Generic MLLMs handle commonsense violations but miss fine-grained anomalies, as Qwen3.5-397B reaches 94.5% on commonsense but only 54.1% on audio. Lacking specialized forensic tools, CoT detectors also degrade sharply, with DeepTraceReward <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite> near chance at 51.9–55.5% across all five categories and BusterX++ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> at 49.9% on audio. In contrast, WeVisForensics stays within 97.0–98.8% across all five categories and leads VideoVeritas <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite> by 27.7% on audio and 20.9% on average. DTPO improves over the SFT agent on all five categories, most on visual appearance by 4.9% and on OCR by 4.4%, demonstrating balanced detection.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T5.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.T5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:113%;">Sub-agent invocation precision on AgenticCue<span id="S5.T5.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (%). Fraction of the
generated videos on which a tool is invoked that are annotated with its category.
#Calls is the average number of executed tool invocations per video.</span></span></figcaption>
