</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Ablation Studies</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 5.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> isolates the fast and slow components of DTPO and yields three observations. First, optimizing the main policy against a frozen library mainly fits the training distribution. GRPO gains 2.9% on GB and 2.8% on GB++ over SFT, but only 1.3% on MintVid and 0.4% on AgenticCue. Adding CLUE under the same frozen library moves the average by only 0.5%, because static sub-agents remain an evidence bottleneck. Second, slow sub-agent evolution breaks this bottleneck and drives out-of-domain transfer, lifting the average by 1.6% over GRPO, with gains of 2.3% on MintVid and 2.7% on AgenticCue. Third, action-level credit becomes effective once it is paired with an evolving library, adding a further 1.4% on MintVid and reaching the best overall average of 95.2%, ahead of SFT by 3.9% and GRPO by 2.0%. Publishing the refined library every rollout batch instead of every <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H{=}20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H{=}20</annotation></semantics></math> steps also hurts transfer, lowering every unseen generator by up to 4.8% and the OOD mean by 2.0% in Table <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 5.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. The two processes are thus complementary, provided the library is refreshed at a stable cadence.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T6.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.T6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:113%;">Component ablation.<span id="S5.T6.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> All variants start from the same SFT agent and FSL, train on the same RL pool. Accuracy (%) follows the protocol of Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Evaluation on standard benchmarks. ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. Agentic is the mean accuracy over the five AgenticCue categories. Avg. averages GB, GB++, MintVid, and Agentic.</span></span></figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T7.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="S5.T7.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Update cadence of the forensic library.<span id="S5.T7.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> <span id="S5.T7.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Left:</span> accuracy (%) on unseen OOD generators comparing refreshing the library every <math id="S5.T7.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H{=}20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H{=}20</annotation></semantics></math> steps as in DTPO, refreshing it on every rollout batch, and a staged schedule that first evolves the library and then freezes it while training the main agent. All start from the same SFT agent and library and are evaluated at the same step, and <math id="S5.T7.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is DTPO minus each alternative. <span id="S5.T7.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Right:</span> training reward against wall-clock time.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Slow-fast training is effective.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 5.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> compares DTPO with two alternative schedules from the same SFT initialization. Refreshing the library on every rollout batch lowers accuracy on all six unseen OOD generators, with drops of 4.8% on Hailuo, 2.6% on Kling, and 2.3% on Sora2, reducing the six-generator mean by 2.0% despite similar training rewards. The staged schedule first evolves the library and then freezes it while training the main agent, so both levels improve but never adapt to each other. DTPO still leads it on every unseen generator, by 2.4% on the six-generator mean, as co-evolution lifts fake recall across unseen generators from 70.2% under the staged schedule and 71.3% under every-step refresh to 74.8% while preserving 100% real-video recall. Strengthening the inspectors first or refreshing them on every batch thus fails to recover the out-of-domain transfer of two-timescale co-evolution.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Does Sub-agent Evolution Improve Evidence?</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Video-level accuracy cannot separate a better inspection policy from better sub-agent responses. Table <a href="#S5.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 5.4 Does Sub-agent Evolution Improve Evidence? ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> therefore scores sub-agent calls against role-level annotations that mark which roles are worth inspecting on each test video and over which interval. Two cross-family VLM annotators label each video independently, and a label-blind judge resolves their disagreements. The evolving library sharpens the evidence of all three roles. The physical sub-agent improves on every benchmark, by 9.1–31.3%, rising from 66.5% to 97.8% on GB as its inconclusive rate falls from 26.9% to 0.3%. On the unseen MintVid generators, appearance and physical F1 rise by 7.0% and 19.2%, and OCR evidence improves on every benchmark, by up to 11.8% on GB++. A matched human review (Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>) agrees, preferring the evolved responses in 65 pairs against 20 and cutting responses with any flaw from 30.5% to 8.0%. Unlike a frozen library, the evolving one thus improves the evidence itself, not only how the main agent uses it during investigation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T8.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="S5.T8.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:113%;">Sub-agent evidence quality.<span id="S5.T8.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Sub-agent F1 (%) against role-level annotations. A call counts when its role is annotated and its window overlaps the interval. Both libraries answer the same matched calls. Frozen: SFT library in GRPO. Evolving: refined by DTPO. OCR excludes text-presence routing.</span></span></figcaption>

<td id="S5.T8.8.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E0E0E0;padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;"><span id="S5.T8.8.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#E0E0E0;">Evolving</span></td>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Evaluation on AgenticCue. ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> asks whether the main agent invokes the role a video calls for. Querying every tool on every video only attains the base rate, which limits ARGUS to 78.6% on physical consistency. WeVisForensics instead reaches 94.3–99.7% precision on the physical, OCR, commonsense, and audio roles, 1.2–4.4 times their base rates, and DTPO improves physical precision by 0.6% and both OCR and commonsense precision by 22.6% over the SFT agent. Precision does not require exhaustive calls, as DTPO learns which inspector is informative and issues 12.4% fewer calls than SFT yet gains accuracy on every AgenticCue category.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/visualevo.png" id="S5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/253;" width="467" height="253" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F5.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.F5.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Self-evolution of the forensic library over training.<span id="S5.F5.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> </span>(a)<span id="S5.F5.10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Sub-agent verdicts on training calls, scored against role-level annotations. Left: moving averages of the miss rate on generated videos and of the verdict F1 over LoRA refreshes (minor ticks). Middle: role-level error per sub-agent across the early, middle, and late phases of training. Right: evidence F1 of the frozen library and of the evolved library at the early, middle, and final checkpoints on four test benchmarks, each spanning the appearance, physical, and OCR axes clockwise. </span>(b)<span id="S5.F5.10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Accepted edits, with one <span id="S5.F5.10.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Report</span> and one <span id="S5.F5.10.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Ignore</span> rule each. The gray card shows candidate rules that failed the acceptance test. </span>(c)<span id="S5.F5.10.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Three generated test videos inspected by the three checkpoints, with verbatim sub-agent excerpts and the agent’s final answer.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Visualizing Self-Evolution</h3>

<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/motivation-2.png" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/247;" width="476" height="247" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Qualitative comparison on a generated video with warping handwritten text.<span id="S5.F6.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> <span id="S5.F6.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Left:</span> <span id="S5.F6.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a)</span> The CoT-based VideoVeritas <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite> dismisses the garbled text as stylistic without inspecting it. <span id="S5.F6.9.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">b)</span> In the fixed-workflow ARGUS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite>, texture, lighting, and motion reports outweigh the detected text deformation. <span id="S5.F6.9.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Right:</span> The SFT or DTPO-trained main agent paired with the SFT or evolved sub-agents. The evolved sub-agents flag the glyph anomalies, and only the trained main agent, which moves its OCR inspection to the warped text at 7 s, turns them into a fake verdict.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Both levels contribute.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Both levels contribute. ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> crosses the SFT and DTPO-trained main agents with the SFT and evolved libraries, the pairings illustrated in Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>. Evolving the library alone lifts the SFT investigator from 91.3% to 92.0%, and training the investigator alone reaches 93.2%. Evolving both reaches 95.2%, a gain of 3.9% that exceeds the sum of the two single-level gains by 1.3%. The two levels are therefore complementary: the trained investigator issues more targeted calls, and the evolved inspectors make each of those calls more informative.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T9" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T9.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.T9.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:113%;">Contribution of each level to investigator–inspector co-evolution.<span id="S5.T9.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The investigator and inspectors before (SFT) or after (DTPO) co-evolution are paired in all four combinations, reporting average accuracy (%) over GB, GB++, MintVid, and AgenticCue. Evolving either level alone helps, and evolving both gives the largest gain.</span></span></figcaption>
<table id="S5.T9.8" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S5.T9.8.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T9.8.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T9.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Investigator <math id="S5.T9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\backslash" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>\</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\backslash</annotation></semantics></math> Inspectors</span></td>
<td id="S5.T9.8.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T9.8.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">SFT</span></td>
<td id="S5.T9.8.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T9.8.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">DTPO</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T9.8.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T9.8.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T9.8.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">SFT</span></td>
<td id="S5.T9.8.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T9.8.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">91.3</span></td>
<td id="S5.T9.8.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T9.8.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">92.0</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T9.8.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T9.8.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="S5.T9.8.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">DTPO</span></td>
<td id="S5.T9.8.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S5.T9.8.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">93.2</span></td>
<td id="S5.T9.8.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S5.T9.8.3.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">95.2</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5.4 Does Sub-agent Evolution Improve Evidence? ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> traces the forensic library through training at three levels. At the parameter level, successive LoRA refreshes cut the missed anomalies on generated videos from 22.1% to 5.2% while false alarms on real videos also decline and verdict F1 rises from 80.3% to 93.7%, and every sub-agent errs progressively less across the early, middle, and late phases, with the OCR error falling from 24.7% to 9.3%. On the test benchmarks, the final library delivers higher evidence F1 than the frozen one along all three axes. At the prompt level, accepted skill-card edits add reporting rules to the appearance and commonsense sub-agents. At the case level, the same inspection returns different evidence over training. The early sub-agent calls each scene coherent and the agent answers real, whereas the final sub-agent names the regenerating texture, the color-shifting paint stream, or the rigid milk stream, and the agent answers fake. Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> shows the same effect at the agent level, where only the evolved sub-agents confirm the artifact. The gains thus come from sub-agents that learn to report artifacts they once called coherent.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">A qualitative example.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.5 Visualizing Self-Evolution ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> follows one generated video whose handwritten text warps as the clip proceeds. VideoVeritas dismisses the garbled text as stylistic without inspecting it, and in ARGUS the texture, lighting, and motion reports outweigh the detected text deformation. Within WeVisForensics, the SFT sub-agents judge the text structurally regular under either main agent. The evolved sub-agents flag its glyph anomalies, yet the SFT main agent still attributes them to hand-drawn styling and answers real. Only the DTPO-trained main agent, which targets its OCR inspection at the warped text at 7 s, combines this evidence into a fake verdict, so the correction requires both levels to evolve. A complete multi-turn investigation before and after evolution and further comparisons are given in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Additional Evolution Comparisons ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>, and a full trajectory in Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Qualitative Example of the Inspection Process ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Qualitative Example of the Inspection Process</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#S5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 5.6 Qualitative Example of the Inspection Process ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>–<a href="#S5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 5.6 Qualitative Example of the Inspection Process ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> show complete interactions of the final WeVisForensics checkpoint on three generated videos: the main agent’s reasoning and chosen inspection (scope in seconds), the response of the invoked sub-agent, and the final verdict. Text is reproduced verbatim from the model outputs, with only formatting changes. The three examples are decided by OCR, audio, and commonsense and physical evidence, respectively, and Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Additional Inspection Examples ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> gives three more, including a real video.</p>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="1096.21" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 1096.21" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,1096.21) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 7.01 L 0 1089.2 C 0 1093.07 3.14 1096.21 7.01 1096.21 L 646.14 1096.21 C 650.01 1096.21 653.15 1093.07 653.15 1089.2 L 653.15 7.01 C 653.15 3.14 650.01 0 646.14 0 L 7.01 0 C 3.14 0 0 3.14 0 7.01 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 7.01 L 1.11 1076.28 L 652.04 1076.28 L 652.04 7.01 C 652.04 3.75 649.4 1.11 646.14 1.11 L 7.01 1.11 C 3.75 1.11 1.11 3.75 1.11 7.01 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 14.89 1083.48)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:45.97em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.16em;font-size:10pt;" height="9.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 7.69)" width="636.1"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:45.97em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Investigation trace: repeated glyph distortion</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 14.89 10.95)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:53em;--ltx-fo-height:76.42em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="1057.47" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 1057.47)" width="733.37"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:53em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 1 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">visual_appearance[0.0--5.9 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The primary hypothesis is that the sequence may contain a localized temporal rendering defect rather than a globally unstable scene. The overview shows one apparent speaker, a phone, four product boxes, and a hand moving across the foreground, so the most useful first check is a full-range visual comparison across the entire 5.875-second interval. This can establish whether object boundaries, textures, lighting, and motion remain coherent as the hand approaches and leaves the boxes. I will therefore inspect the complete range with the visual-appearance skill, using the sampled progression rather than relying on a single frame. The result should distinguish ordinary motion blur or occlusion from abrupt changes in an object’s shape or surface detail. At this stage, the repeated packaging and stable background provide useful reference points, while the moving hand remains the main area requiring scrutiny. Any anomaly found here would motivate a more targeted examination of the visible printed text.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="184.53" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 184.53" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,184.53) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="171.12" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 168.97)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">issue<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (medium)</span></span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. The clearest appearance concern is the unusually smooth, rendered quality of the woman’s face during the opening pointing gesture. Across the changing head positions, the forehead, cheeks, and nose retain broad, nearly textureless tonal gradients, while the eyes, eyebrows, and lip contours remain comparatively crisp. The cheek coloration also appears softly blended into the surrounding skin rather than showing comparable fine surface detail. This produces a waxy, airbrushed appearance that persists as the face moves, rather than being confined to one blurred pose. The effect is most apparent when the face is exposed between the moving arm and the phone. Confidence is medium because cosmetic smoothing and image processing can produce similar cues, and the frames do not establish a separate, unmistakable boundary failure.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 2 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ocr_consistency[@ 4.0 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The preceding full-range appearance review identifies a medium-confidence concern involving the face’s unusually smooth, rendered-looking surface, but it does not establish a decisive boundary failure and leaves cosmetic processing as a plausible alternative. The remaining useful question is whether the prominent product packaging behaves like stable physical text. The overview shows four nearly identical boxes with repeated lettering, making a focused OCR-consistency check at 4.0 seconds appropriate: it can compare the legibility and structure of the printed regions while the boxes are clearly visible. This targeted scope is useful because generated imagery often produces malformed or inconsistent glyphs even when the surrounding scene appears coherent. I will use the OCR skill at that timestamp, including its localized text assessment, to test whether the repeated labels retain plausible character shapes and spacing. This evidence should be weighed alongside, rather than substituted for, the earlier appearance finding.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="167.8" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 167.8" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,167.8) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 167.8 L 623.38 167.8 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 167.8 L 623.38 167.8 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:12.94em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="154.39" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 152.24)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">text suspicious<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (medium)</span></span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;">Issues:</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> Repeated central A glyphs have unusually narrow upper structures and elongated lower diagonals; The repeated label has inconsistent character construction despite broadly similar lettering. </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;">Reason:</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> All three crops show a recurring localized anomaly in the central A. The concern is its distorted construction, not the unusual spelling or OCR mismatch. Softness limits certainty, but the repeated structural irregularity supports a suspicious assessment.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 3 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p7.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent: final verdict  <span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p7.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">answer(fake)</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p8.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="189.29" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 189.29" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,189.29) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 189.29 L 623.38 189.29 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 189.29 L 623.38 189.29 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.77em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="175.89" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 173.73)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p8.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Verdict.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p3.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> The evidence supports a fake classification. Across the full sequence, the visual review found a persistent waxy, airbrushed quality in the woman’s face: broad textureless gradients coexist with comparatively crisp eyes, brows, and lips. This is a meaningful rendering concern, though its medium confidence and the possibility of cosmetic smoothing or image processing limit its decisiveness. The focused text review independently found recurring structural irregularities in the repeated central “A” glyphs, including narrow upper forms and elongated lower diagonals, with inconsistent character construction across similar labels. That result is also medium confidence because softness can obscure fine detail, but the anomaly recurs across multiple localized regions rather than being a single ambiguous crop. Together, the persistent facial rendering artifact and repeated malformed packaging text provide converging signs of synthetic image generation. No audio is available, so there is no speech or voice evidence to weigh. The combined visual and text inconsistencies outweigh the stated uncertainty and favor fake.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span></span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="1344.52" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 1344.52" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,1344.52) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 7.01 L 0 1337.51 C 0 1341.38 3.14 1344.52 7.01 1344.52 L 646.14 1344.52 C 650.01 1344.52 653.15 1341.38 653.15 1337.51 L 653.15 7.01 C 653.15 3.14 650.01 0 646.14 0 L 7.01 0 C 3.14 0 0 3.14 0 7.01 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 7.01 L 1.11 1324.59 L 652.04 1324.59 L 652.04 7.01 C 652.04 3.75 649.4 1.11 646.14 1.11 L 7.01 1.11 C 3.75 1.11 1.11 3.75 1.11 7.01 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 14.89 1331.79)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:45.97em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.16em;font-size:10pt;" height="9.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 7.69)" width="636.1"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:45.97em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Investigation trace: voice–face mismatch</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 14.89 10.95)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:53em;--ltx-fo-height:94.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="1305.79" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 1305.79)" width="733.37"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:53em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 1 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">visual_appearance[0.0--8.0 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The primary hypothesis is that the sequence may contain temporal rendering artifacts rather than merely ordinary camera motion. The supplied overview shows one apparent woman on a wooden bridge across eight seconds, with repeated close views of her face, hair, clothing, and the surrounding railing. A full-range visual appearance inspection is therefore the most useful first step: it can compare identity-bearing details across closely spaced samples while also checking whether the background remains geometrically stable. I will examine the entire 0.0–8.0 second interval rather than a single frame, because generation artifacts often appear as localized changes in facial structure, hair boundaries, or texture that are not visible in isolated images. This scope also allows the tool to distinguish plausible changes caused by pose, focus, lighting, or motion from abrupt inconsistencies that persist despite a largely continuous scene. The result should establish whether there is a concrete visual anomaly before considering the audio evidence.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="184.53" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 184.53" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,184.53) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="171.12" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 168.97)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">issue<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (medium)</span></span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. The face has a conspicuously soft, rendered appearance across the opening portion. The forehead, cheeks, and nose form unusually uniform, low-texture surfaces, while the eyes, eyebrows, and red lip contours remain comparatively crisp. This contrast persists as the head changes angle and the mouth changes shape, giving the facial surface a smoothed, synthetic quality rather than simply making the entire image uniformly soft. The effect is most apparent in the early frontal and slightly turned views, where the surrounding hair strands, ribbed collar, and wooden railing retain more distinct detail. The anomaly is primarily the persistent facial rendering quality, not a definite change in identity or a major boundary failure. Confidence is medium because cosmetic smoothing and image processing can produce some similar characteristics.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 2 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">voice_profile</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The visual inspection has established a medium-confidence concern involving the facial rendering, but that observation alone does not determine whether the media is synthetic because smoothing, compression, or post-processing can create similar effects. The next useful check is the audio, especially because the overview presents one apparent person whose mouth is visibly changing across the sequence. A speaker-aware voice profile can characterize whether the audio contains one coherent speaker and provide descriptive age and gender estimates that may support or conflict with the visible subject. This is not a standalone authenticity test, and the analysis should be discounted if there are multiple speakers, dubbing, voice-over, or weak speaker-to-face correspondence. I will therefore request the profile for the whole video, preserving the full temporal scope so any segmentation or overlap information is available. The purpose is to add an independent modality while keeping the visual anomaly as the main working hypothesis.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="416.72" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 416.72" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,416.72) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 416.72 L 623.38 416.72 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 416.72 L 623.38 416.72 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:34.11em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="403.32" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 401.17)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 3 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p7.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent: final verdict  <span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p7.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">answer(fake)</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p8.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="189.29" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 189.29" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,189.29) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 189.29 L 623.38 189.29 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 189.29 L 623.38 189.29 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.77em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="175.89" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 173.73)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p8.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Verdict.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p6.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> The evidence favors a fake classification. The full-range visual analysis found a persistent, medium-confidence rendering issue: the face appears unusually soft and uniformly low-textured while the eyes, brows, lips, hair, collar, and railing retain sharper detail. That selective smoothing is consistent with synthetic facial rendering, although cosmetic processing remains a plausible limited alternative, so the visual result is not decisive by itself. The audio profile is formally informational rather than an authenticity verdict, but it reports a single speaker with estimated ages of 45 and 39 and male probabilities of 1.00, while the visible, apparently speaking subject is clearly a young woman. This is a concrete age and gender conflict across both detected segments. Dubbing or uncertain correspondence could weaken it, but the overview shows one unambiguous visible speaker and no reported overlap, making the mismatch meaningful supporting evidence. Together, the visual artifact and strong voice-to-face inconsistency outweigh the stated uncertainty.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 1 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">common_sense[9.4--15.1 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The visible sequence presents a highly unusual airport event: a decorated passenger aircraft appears to be moving alongside a large Santa sleigh filled with gifts. Before assessing whether the imagery is physically credible, it is useful to test the scene against ordinary event logic. The key hypothesis is that the apparent flight may be a staged visual effect, a composited sequence, or an AI-generated depiction rather than a genuine recording. This common-sense review should examine whether the aircraft, sleigh, airport infrastructure, and their apparent relationship form a plausible real-world scenario. It should also distinguish merely fantastical subject matter from contradictions in the depicted event, such as unsupported objects, unexplained attachments, or actions that require impossible mechanics. The selected interval covers the transition from the close ground-level views to the wider airborne views, making it appropriate for evaluating the central causal claim without relying only on isolated visual artifacts.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="167.92" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 167.92" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,167.92) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 167.92 L 623.38 167.92 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 167.92 L 623.38 167.92 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:12.95em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="154.51" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 152.36)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">issue<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (high)</span></span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. The scene depicts a commercial passenger aircraft taking off from an airport runway while carrying a large red sleigh filled with presents and a Santa-like figure. The sleigh is positioned behind the aircraft and appears to travel with it, but no visible mechanism explains how the sleigh is attached, supported, or propelled. The aircraft’s ordinary flight behavior is therefore combined with an unexplained passenger-carrying vehicle that has no plausible operational role in the scene. The Christmas trees and decorations fit a festive theme, but they do not provide a causal explanation for the sleigh’s movement or the aircraft’s unusual load. The event is clearly visible across multiple frames, making the semantic and causal inconsistency sufficiently observable.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 2 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">physical_consistency[9.4--15.1 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The preceding semantic review identifies a strong causal concern: the sleigh appears to accompany the aircraft without an evident explanation for its support or propulsion. That finding supports a more focused physical examination, but it does not by itself establish whether the apparent motion is a practical stunt, an edit, or generated imagery. The next useful test is therefore physical consistency across the same late sequence. This review should track the aircraft’s trajectory, the sleigh’s position and orientation, the apparent connection between them, and whether their motion remains mechanically coherent as the camera perspective changes. It should also check for continuity in the aircraft’s structure and the sleigh’s relationship to the surrounding airport environment. Because the available interval is sampled rather than continuous, the assessment should remain attentive to uncertainty about unseen attachment points, forces, and intermediate motion, while still determining whether the visible dynamics provide a credible real-world explanation.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="184.53" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 184.53" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,184.53) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="171.12" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 168.97)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">issue<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (high)</span></span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. The aircraft and sleigh do not maintain physically plausible contact or motion relationships. The sleigh appears to travel alongside and then behind the aircraft while remaining suspended above the tarmac, with no visible support, propulsion, or mechanically credible connection. Across the sequence, the aircraft rises and advances while the sleigh stays at a similar height and follows a separate path, despite the apparent proximity and alignment suggesting a shared movement. The sleigh also passes close to the aircraft without a clear collision response or consistent depth relationship. The reindeer antlers on the aircraft are visible, but they do not provide a plausible mechanism for pulling or carrying the sleigh. These are clear violations of contact, trajectory, and object-motion consistency rather than ordinary camera movement or a normal airport maneuver.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 3 </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p7.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent: final verdict  <span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p7.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">answer(fake)</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p8.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="170.54" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 170.54" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,170.54) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 170.54 L 623.38 170.54 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 170.54 L 623.38 170.54 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 6.7)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:13.36em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="157.13" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 157.13)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p8.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Verdict.</span><span id="S5.SS6.p9.pic1.p8.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> Both analyses independently identify high-confidence problems in the central event. The common-sense assessment finds that a commercial passenger aircraft appears to take off while carrying or traveling with a large red sleigh and Santa-like figure, but no visible mechanism explains how the sleigh is supported, attached, or propelled. The physical-consistency assessment reinforces this: the sleigh follows a separate path while remaining at a similar height, lacks credible contact or motion relationships, and passes near the aircraft without a consistent depth or collision response. The antlers are decorative and do not supply a plausible pulling mechanism. The festive decorations and airport setting are coherent in isolation, but they do not resolve the impossible load and motion. Although sampled frames leave some intermediate behavior unobserved, the repeated causal and physical contradictions across the interval are substantial. The media is therefore best classified as fake.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span></span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S5.SS6.p10.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">
          
<figure id="S5.F9" class="ltx_figure">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.F9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Passenger aircraft and airborne sleigh in a generated airport scene.<span id="S5.F9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ground truth: fake; WeVisForensics prediction: fake; 16.0 s, with audio. Commonsense and physical sub-agents both flag the unsupported airborne sleigh and its decoupled trajectory over <math id="S5.F9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[9.4,15.1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>9.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[9.4,15.1]</annotation></semantics></math> s.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
        
</div>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>AI-Generated Video Detection</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Early detectors treat the task as binary classification over generation traces in images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite> and videos <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>, outputting a score without verifiable evidence, and benchmarks such as GVD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, GenVideo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, GenVidBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>, and AIGVDBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite> scale up binary evaluation across generators. Building on MLLM-based image forensics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>, <a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>, <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, recent video detectors pair each verdict with a natural-language account of the observed artifacts. Methods such as BusterX <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>, BusterX++ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, and VidGuard-R1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> train this reasoning with reinforcement learning, while Skyra <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>, VideoVeritas <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, and VidForensics-M1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite> strengthen it with artifact grounding, perception pretext tasks, and temporal-grounding rewards, respectively. IVY-FAKE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite> and Omni-Fake <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> provide annotated data for explainable detection, while OmniVL-Guard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> unifies detection and grounding across text, images, and videos. However, these detector-centered formulations do not learn when to request a specialized follow-up inspection or how to adapt it to intermediate observations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Agent-Based Forensic Reasoning</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">General video agents query specialized models to gather evidence over long inputs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>, <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>, while forensic agents organize analysis through explicit tools or specialized roles. Tool-augmented detectors such as ClueAegis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, OmniVL-Guard Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>, and TUE-Detector <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite> train a single MLLM to invoke specific toolchains or visual operations such as cropping, zooming, and segmentation. Multi-agent methods such as SafeGuard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, Hermes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>, and DVAR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite> instead distribute evidence extraction, verification, and deliberation across specialized agents. ARGUS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite> and Deepfake-Agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> further train a judge or aggregator over fixed expert agents. However, the invoked experts in these designs never learn from the interactions they serve while the coordinating policy is trained, leaving the experts’ forensic response policies outside the ongoing policy-learning loop.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents WeVisForensics, an agentic framework for AI-generated video detection in which an investigator coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspectors. Within this framework, DTPO is introduced to optimize the investigator on a fast timescale while refining the inspectors from its calls on a slow one. To support training and evaluation, ForenCue-30K is constructed with role-specific supervision and executed trajectories, and AgenticCue is established to assess both detection verdicts and the inspections behind them. Extensive experiments across benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of WeVisForensics, highlighting the value of co-evolving the investigator with its inspectors.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
