<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Implementation Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training and inference setup.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The main agent and the four visual sub-agents are rank-64 LoRA adapters on a shared Qwen3.5-4B backbone, initialized from SFT adapters trained on 33,896 interaction trajectories and 117,552 role-specific records, while the base Qwen3.5-4B serves as the frozen CLUE reference <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The main agent observes up to 16 uniformly sampled frames of the full video, and each window-based visual sub-agent inspects its requested window at 2 FPS, whereas the OCR sub-agent inspects the frame at its requested timestamp and the two audio tools analyze the whole soundtrack in Sec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Forensic Sub-agent Library ‣ 2 WeVisForensics Agent Framework ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>. In the fast process, GRPO samples <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G{=}4</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts per video with 32 videos per batch and at most 4 sub-agent calls per trajectory for one epoch over the RL pool, and the main-agent learning rate warms up linearly to <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>. CLUE uses <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon{=}0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon{=}0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. (<a href="#S4.E10" title="Equation 10 ‣ Fast process: investigator policy learning. ‣ 4.2 Stage II: DTPO ‣ 4 Training Pipeline ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>) and call-advantage weight <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda{=}0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda{=}0.2</annotation></semantics></math>, and the tool-coverage F1 bonus has weight <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math>. In the slow process, calls with utility below <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa{=}{-}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa{=}{-}0.05</annotation></semantics></math> are relabeled as hedges, and each visual sub-agent’s adapter is refreshed every <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H{=}20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H{=}20</annotation></semantics></math> main-agent steps on class-balanced batches of 32 grounded calls, with the sub-agent learning rate decayed linearly from <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> over training progress, decision-token weight <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, label-correction weight <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>, and teacher EMA rate <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho{=}0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho{=}0.001</annotation></semantics></math>. The audio tools remain fixed during training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">AgenticCue composition and evaluation metrics.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AgenticCue comprises <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}830" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,830</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}830</annotation></semantics></math> unique videos in total: <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,330</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}330</annotation></semantics></math> unique generated videos and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> fixed real videos. Each of the five forensic categories (<span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Visual</span>, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Physical</span>, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">OCR</span>, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Common sense</span>, and <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Audio</span>) contains exactly <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> generated videos verified to exhibit that category’s artifact (<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="170" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>170</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">170</annotation></semantics></math> generated videos carry annotations for more than one category, yielding <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,330</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}330</annotation></semantics></math> unique generated clips across the five <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math>-clip category sets). For category <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, binary detection accuracy (<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Acc.}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext>Acc.</mtext><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Acc.}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>) is evaluated under a balanced 1:1 pairing of its <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> generated videos and the <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> real videos (<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> videos per category), counting invalid or missing outputs as errors. Sub-agent invocation precision (<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Prec.}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext>Prec.</mtext><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Prec.}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>) measures whether the agent calls the relevant tool for its artifact: computed at the video level over the full pool of generated videos, with <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Prec.}_{s}=|C_{s}\cap G_{s}|/|C_{s}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>Prec.</mtext><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Prec.}_{s}=|C_{s}\cap G_{s}|/|C_{s}|</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set on which the agent invokes tool <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> at least once and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of videos that call for role <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. Two label systems are involved. The <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math>-clip category membership above only defines the accuracy subsets, and a clip assigned to one category can still exhibit artifacts of other roles. <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> for the four visual roles therefore comes from the dense role annotations of Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, where two cross-family VLM annotators independently mark every role worth inspecting on each generated video and a label-blind judge resolves disagreements. Two videos without a resolved annotation are excluded, leaving <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}328" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,328</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}328</annotation></semantics></math> eligible videos for the visual roles. These annotations do not cover audio, so <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> for audio is the <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math>-clip Audio category over all <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,330</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}330</annotation></semantics></math> generated videos. An agent that invokes tool <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> on every eligible video attains the base rate <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|G_{s}|/|\text{eligible}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mtext>eligible</mtext><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|G_{s}|/|\text{eligible}|</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="91.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>91.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">91.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>78.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.6\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>49.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>21.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the appearance, physical, OCR, commonsense, and audio roles. Table <a href="#S3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Metrics. ‣ 3.2 AgenticCue Benchmark ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> summarizes these label counts. Precision is read together with category accuracy, which would drop if the agent skipped relevant inspections. DTPO raises accuracy on every AgenticCue category (Table <a href="#A3.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ Detection improves across evaluated categories. ‣ Appendix C Detailed Detection Results ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>), including OCR, commonsense, and audio.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Human Review of Annotations</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Role-specific evidence annotations and main-agent interaction trajectories are produced by model annotators and coupled with human feedback (Figure <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) before entering the training records of Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Data Construction ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. During prompt development and source onboarding, human reviewers inspect sampled annotations per source and role, flagging hallucinated explanations, over-generalized commonsense claims, imprecise temporal windows, or redundant/omitted tool calls. These failure modes are fed back to refine the annotation prompts and filtering rules, while unplayable clips are discarded. For the audio role, reviewers work through a per-source queue, watch each video with its audio, and record whether the soundtrack is inconsistent with the visible speech along with the offending interval (Figure <a href="#A2.F11.sf1" title="Figure 11(a) ‣ Figure 11 ‣ Paired review of evolved sub-agent evidence. ‣ Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11(a)</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Quantitative human audit of sub-agent annotations and main-agent trajectories.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To quantify the quality of the resulting supervision in ForenCue-30K, we conduct two model-assisted human verification audits (fixed random seed <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math>), summarized in Figure <a href="#A2.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Quantitative human audit of sub-agent annotations and main-agent trajectories. ‣ Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>:</p>
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sub-agent role annotations (Figure <a href="#A2.F10.sf1" title="Figure 10(a) ‣ Figure 10 ‣ Quantitative class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10(a)</span></a>):</span> We audit <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="340" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>340</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">340</annotation></semantics></math> video–role annotations on <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> generated training videos across all four visual specialist roles (<math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Visual appearance</span>, <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" consistency</span>, <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">OCR consistency</span> on clips). For each video–role pair, the auditor watches the full video and rates the distilled verdict, temporal interval, and explanation as <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Correct &amp; Supported</span> (accurately describes a visually observable artifact within the stated window), <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Partially Correct</span> (appropriate verdict with minor explanation or boundary imprecision), or <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Incorrect</span> (hallucinated or contradicted by the video). Overall, <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation annotations are at least partially supported by visual evidence (<math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.7\%" display="inline" alttext="322/340" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>322</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>340</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">322/340</annotation></semantics></math>] fully supported and <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation <span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">OCR</span>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Main-agent tool-selection trajectories (Figure <a href="#A2.F10.sf2" title="Figure 10(b) ‣ Figure 10 ‣ Quantitative human audit of sub-agent annotations and main-agent trajectories. ‣ Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10(b)</span></a>):</span> We audit <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> deduplicated main-agent SFT trajectories (comprising <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="209" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>209</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">209</annotation></semantics></math> sub-agent invocations across the six forensic roles). For each trajectory, the auditor watches the video with audio, inspects the sequence of invoked tools and returned observations, and judges whether the tool selection is appropriate or suffers from omitted or redundant role invocations. Across the <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> trajectories, <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.0\%</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> (<math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96/100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96/100</annotation></semantics></math>)</span> are judged to have appropriate tool selection (<math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> [<math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49/50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>49</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49/50</annotation></semantics></math>] on generated videos and <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>94.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> [<math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="47/50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>47</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">47/50</annotation></semantics></math>] on real videos). Only <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> trajectories exhibit minor selection issues (<math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Physical</span>, and <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> redundant <span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">OCR</span> call), corresponding to a call-level precision of <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation <section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Paired review of evolved sub-agent evidence.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Verdict accuracy alone does not show whether evolution improves the evidence a sub-agent reports. We pair <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math> inspections from the evaluation benchmarks, each answered by the SFT and the evolved sub-agent under the same main agent and inspection window. The pairs are stratified by role, video label, and verdict agreement. A reviewer sees both responses in random order with model identities hidden (Figure <a href="#A2.F11.sf2" title="Figure 11(b) ‣ Figure 11 ‣ Paired review of evolved sub-agent evidence. ‣ Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11(b)</span></a>), marks which response gives more accurate evidence, and flags in each response unsupported or mislocalized claims and missed visible anomalies. A second reviewer re-checks the judgments. The evolved sub-agents are preferred in <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>65</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65</annotation></semantics></math> pairs against <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>, and the share of responses with any flaw falls from <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> (Table <a href="#A2.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Paired review of evolved sub-agent evidence. ‣ Appendix B Human Review of Annotations ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>). Missed anomalies drop from <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>28.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28.6\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> and nearly vanish for appearance, physical, and OCR alike, while unsupported claims stay rare. Where the two verdicts agree, neither response is rated better in <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>97</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> pairs, so evolution leaves consistent evidence intact and its gains concentrate on the inspections it changes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span><span id="A2.T10.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Paired human review of sub-agent evidence.</span> Each pair answers the same inspection with the SFT (S) and evolved (E) sub-agent. Preferred counts pairs where one response gives more accurate evidence, omitting ties and pairs where both are unreliable. Missed: a clearly visible relevant anomaly is not reported. Flawed: the response misses a visible anomaly or reports one that is unsupported, out of role, or mislocalized. Rates in %.</figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F11.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="A2.F11.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Human review interfaces.<span id="A2.F11.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> </span>(a)<span id="A2.F11.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The reviewer filters the queue by source and review status, watches the full clip, and records whether an audio inconsistency is present, absent, or inconclusive, along with the supporting time interval. </span>(b)<span id="A2.F11.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The reviewer inspects the stated window and compares two anonymized sub-agent responses to the same inspection, marking the more accurate evidence and flagging unsupported claims and missed anomalies in each.</span></span></figcaption>

</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Detailed Detection Results</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section expands the main comparisons along two axes: the quality of the evidence returned by individual sub-agents (Table <a href="#S5.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 5.4 Does Sub-agent Evolution Improve Evidence? ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>), and detection accuracy, fake recall, and F1 across benchmarks and generator categories (Table <a href="#A3.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ Detection improves across evaluated categories. ‣ Appendix C Detailed Detection Results ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sub-agent evidence improves across roles.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Evolving the library improves the evidence returned by every trainable role (Table <a href="#S5.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 5.4 Does Sub-agent Evolution Improve Evidence? ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). The physical sub-agent moves the most, with F1 on GB rising from 66.5% to 97.8%, and the largest gains of the appearance and OCR sub-agents reach 7.0% and 11.8%.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Three patterns explain these gains. First, the physical sub-agent stops hedging. Its inconclusive rate falls on every benchmark, from 26.9% to 0.3% on GB, 12.3% to 0.9% on GB++, 10.5% to 1.2% on MintVid, and 6.4% to 0.4% on AgenticCue, and its F1 rises by 9.1–31.3%. This matches the slow process, which relabels correct but inconclusive low-utility answers as hedges. Second, appearance evidence becomes more decisive. The share of annotated generated calls it flags rises from 96.0% to 99.8% on GB and from 66.0% to 76.2% on MintVid, and its MintVid F1 rises by 7.0%. Third, OCR evidence becomes sharper, with F1 rising on every benchmark and most on GB++ by 11.8%. The gains on the out-of-distribution MintVid, 7.0% for appearance and 19.2% for physical, show that the evolved evidence transfers to unseen generators.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Detection improves across evaluated categories.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to the SFT agent, DTPO improves accuracy on all six MintVid categories and all five AgenticCue categories (Table <a href="#A3.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ Detection improves across evaluated categories. ‣ Appendix C Detailed Detection Results ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>), including an OCR fake-recall increase from 95.0% to 98.4%. Fake recall alone can be misleading. Gemini-3.1-Pro and DeepTraceReward label almost every video as generated, reaching 99.0% and 99.5% fake recall on GB++ but only 54.3% and 58.8% accuracy, whereas WeVisForensics keeps 97.2% fake recall at 97.5% accuracy. Across the 13 evaluated categories, WeVisForensics ranks first in both accuracy and F1 on 12. The largest gains over the SFT agent appear on the unseen MintVid generators, where accuracy rises by 7.5% on Kling, 6.5% on Sora2, and 5.1% on Hailuo.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T11" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 11: </span><span id="A3.T11.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GenBuster-Bench breakdown across official splits and generators.</span> Following the official split organization of BusterX++ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, ID, the eight unseen OOD generators, OOD Mean, and Wild report per-subset forgery detection rate (%), while All reports overall detection accuracy (%) across the full benchmark.</figcaption>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Learned Skill Cards</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section lists the complete skill cards learned by the forensic library across four training runs. Each rule is appended to the user prompt of the corresponding sub-agent alongside the inspection query. <span id="A4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Report</span> rules specify generation artifacts to flag, while <span id="A4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Ignore</span> rules describe benign camera, motion, or compression effects that should not be mistaken for synthesis errors. The learned rules are local and contrastive. A typical <span id="A4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Report</span> rule describes an artifact against an intact reference in the same frame, such as a single fused glyph among sharp neighboring characters or melting facial contours against a sharp background, and the matching <span id="A4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Ignore</span> rule names the global degradation that produces a similar look, such as uniform blur or compression across the whole region. Because each edit is mined from calls that the current inspector still judges wrongly, the cards are specific to the failures of that run and differ in concrete content across runs. For example, the physical card of Run 2 targets finger articulation and garment topology, whereas that of Run 3 targets rigid tools sliding over granular surfaces and morphing sculptures.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Run 1</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A4.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="307.09" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 307.09" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,307.09) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 7.01 L 0 300.08 C 0 303.95 3.14 307.09 7.01 307.09 L 646.14 307.09 C 650.01 307.09 653.15 303.95 653.15 300.08 L 653.15 7.01 C 653.15 3.14 650.01 0 646.14 0 L 7.01 0 C 3.14 0 0 3.14 0 7.01 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 7.01 L 1.11 277.91 L 652.04 277.91 L 652.04 7.01 C 652.04 3.75 649.4 1.11 646.14 1.11 L 7.01 1.11 C 3.75 1.11 1.11 3.75 1.11 7.01 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.41 280.4)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:53.93em;--ltx-fo-height:1.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="24.2" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 24.2)" width="746.24"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R1.<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: Surfaces exhibiting broad, continuous color gradients that completely lack fine micro-texture while adjacent objects retain sharp, distinct edges.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R2.<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Uniform frame-wide softness or compression artifacts that affect the entire scene equally without local texture loss.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R3.<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Motion blur or softness on moving subjects caused by camera movement or subject velocity.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R4.<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Smooth skin surfaces resulting from shallow depth of field, distance, or soft natural lighting that lacks harsh specular highlights.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R5.<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: Facial skin that exhibits a uniform, airbrushed finish lacking pores or micro-texture while adjacent hair and background retain sharp detail.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R6.<span id="A4.p3.pic1.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Silhouetted subjects in strong backlight where facial features are obscured by deep shadow and low contrast.</span></span></span>

<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R1.<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: Rigid objects that change structural shape, length, or thickness during continuous motion or camera panning.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R2.<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Low-resolution softness or motion blur that makes fine details like fingers or distant rigging indistinct.</span></span></span>

<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R4.<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Soft edges or motion blur on small, fast-moving subjects that make their fine structure indistinct.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R5.<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: A subject’s position or pose that shifts abruptly or discontinuously without a corresponding continuous motion trajectory.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R6.<span id="A4.p4.pic1.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Smooth, mannequin-like continuity of a subject’s pose or body during camera movement or panning.</span></span></span>

<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:53.93em;">
<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R1.<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Motion blur that softens a moving subject’s skin or hair boundaries during fast movement.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R2.<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: A subject’s surface lacking fine texture while adjacent high-frequency details remain sharp.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R3.<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Global softness or compression artifacts that uniformly reduce detail across the entire frame.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R4.<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Smooth skin or facial surfaces that lack fine pore detail due to beauty filters or high compression.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R5.<span id="A4.p17.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: Facial or hand contours that locally melt or duplicate while surrounding background details remain sharp.</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="A4.p18" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A4.p18.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="145.2" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 145.2" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,145.2) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 7.01 L 0 138.18 C 0 142.06 3.14 145.2 7.01 145.2 L 646.14 145.2 C 650.01 145.2 653.15 142.06 653.15 138.18 L 653.15 7.01 C 653.15 3.14 650.01 0 646.14 0 L 7.01 0 C 3.14 0 0 3.14 0 7.01 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 7.01 L 1.11 116.02 L 652.04 116.02 L 652.04 7.01 C 652.04 3.75 649.4 1.11 646.14 1.11 L 7.01 1.11 C 3.75 1.11 1.11 3.75 1.11 7.01 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.41 118.51)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:53.93em;--ltx-fo-height:1.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="24.2" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 24.2)" width="746.24"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A4.p18.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:53.93em;">
<span id="A4.p18.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p18.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Commonsense<span id="A4.p18.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">  3 rules</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.41 10.18)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:53.93em;--ltx-fo-height:7.15em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.16em;font-size:10pt;" height="101.07" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 98.92)" width="746.24"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:53.93em;">
<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R1.<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: A character’s body or props shifting into a physically incompatible form or scale during a transition.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R2.<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Report: A physical object appearing on the ground with a spill or impact mark lacking a visible causal action.</span></span></span>
<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R3.<span id="A4.p18.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ignore: Stylized or game-like environments where objects or animals behave according to internal rules.</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Additional Evolution Comparisons</h2>

<figure id="A5.F12" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_floatright" style="width:50%;"><img src="2611.21373v1/compare.png" id="A5.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:238/100;" width="238" height="100" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="A5.F12.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of AI-generated video detection paradigms.<span id="A5.F12.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> a) CoT-based reasoning uses textual rationales. b) Multi-agent workflows follow fixed execution structures. c) WeVisForensics adaptively coordinates sub-agents and evolves them together with the main policy.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Appendix E Additional Evolution Comparisons ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> runs the three paradigms of Figure <a href="#A5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ Appendix E Additional Evolution Comparisons ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> on the same generated street-market clip. All three return fake, yet only the adaptive agent grounds its verdict in evidence that exists in the video. The CoT-based detector asserts that the subject moves backward between <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0</annotation></semantics></math> s and <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.0</annotation></semantics></math> s and snaps into a new pose at <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.5</annotation></semantics></math> s, neither of which happens. The fixed-workflow detector queries four preset observers in parallel, and its judge aggregates reports of an abrupt scene cut at <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math> s and a floating lantern that are equally unsupported. WeVisForensics instead issues two targeted calls. An appearance call over <math id="A5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.0,8.0]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8.0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.0,8.0]</annotation></semantics></math> s finds that the emblem and yellow shapes on the red lantern change contour and placement across frames while its paper ridges stay regular, and it sets aside the soft background crowd as ordinary depth of field. An OCR call at <math id="A5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.0</annotation></semantics></math> s then separates the intact calligraphy of the main sign from localized glyph degradation on the apron text.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F13" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/motivation.png" id="A5.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/156;" width="467" height="156" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F13.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 13</span>: </span><span id="A5.F13.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Qualitative comparison of investigation paradigms.<span id="A5.F13.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> All three approaches classify the generated video as fake. The CoT-based detector makes unsupported motion claims, and the fixed-workflow detector aggregates predefined observer reports. The adaptive agent requests localized appearance and OCR inspections and grounds its verdict in changing emblem contours and degraded apron lettering.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F14" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.21373v1/visual.png" id="A5.F14.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/247;" width="467" height="247" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F14.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 14</span>: </span><span id="A5.F14.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Complete evolution comparison.<span id="A5.F14.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> On an AI-generated video, the CoT-based VideoVeritas and the fixed-workflow ARGUS both answer real. Before DTPO (top right), the appearance sub-agent reports no issue and WeVisForensics answers real. After DTPO (bottom right), the same first inspection localizes soft hand and finger boundaries during the opening gesture, and the main agent answers fake.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ Appendix E Additional Evolution Comparisons ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> isolates what evolution changes on a generated showroom video. VideoVeritas takes the stable lighting and showroom background at face value and answers real. The ARGUS observers do mention airbrushed skin, unstable hand edges, and rigid hair, but these cues are diluted among generic summaries and the judge still answers real. Before and after DTPO, WeVisForensics opens with the same appearance call over <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,4.1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,4.1]</annotation></semantics></math> s. The SFT sub-agent returns <span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no_issue</span>, a follow-up voice-profile check finds no anomaly, and the agent answers real. The evolved sub-agent returns <span id="A5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">issue</span> on the identical call, locating soft and indistinct hand and finger boundaries as the speaker extends both arms. The main agent follows up with a physical-consistency check rather than an audio tool and answers fake. Sharper evidence on the same first query thus reverses the verdict and redirects the rest of the investigation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Additional Inspection Examples</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A6.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Appendix F Additional Inspection Examples ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>–<a href="#A6.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ Appendix F Additional Inspection Examples ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> give three further complete investigations in the format of Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Qualitative Example of the Inspection Process ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent forOmni AI-Generated Video Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>, covering appearance, physical, commonsense, and OCR evidence on generated videos and a real recording.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><img src="2611.21373v1/serum_ocr_film.png" id="A6.p2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/67;" width="476" height="67" alt="[Uncaptioned image]">
</div>
<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="1493" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 1493" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,1493) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 7.01 L 0 1485.99 C 0 1489.86 3.14 1493 7.01 1493 L 646.14 1493 C 650.01 1493 653.15 1489.86 653.15 1485.99 L 653.15 7.01 C 653.15 3.14 650.01 0 646.14 0 L 7.01 0 C 3.14 0 0 3.14 0 7.01 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 7.01 L 1.11 1473.07 L 652.04 1473.07 L 652.04 7.01 C 652.04 3.75 649.4 1.11 646.14 1.11 L 7.01 1.11 C 3.75 1.11 1.11 3.75 1.11 7.01 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 14.89 1480.27)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:45.97em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.16em;font-size:10pt;" height="9.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 7.69)" width="636.1"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:45.97em;">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Investigation trace: garbled product label</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 14.89 10.95)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:53em;--ltx-fo-height:105.1em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="1454.26" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 1454.26)" width="733.37"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:53em;">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 1 </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="A6.p3.pic1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">visual_appearance[0.0--5.0 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The sequence shows one apparent presenter demonstrating a cosmetic bottle in a retail-like setting, with the camera moving from a wider view toward a close view. The main hypothesis is that the media may be synthetic if fine details fail to remain stable during this motion, especially on the bottle, dropper, hands, face, and background display. A full-range visual appearance inspection is therefore the most useful first step: it can compare object boundaries, textures, and local details across the entire five-second interval rather than relying on a single frame. This scope also helps distinguish ordinary motion blur or changing perspective from details that appear to regenerate or deform. The result should establish whether there is a broad temporal appearance concern and identify any specific regions that warrant more targeted physical or text-focused examination.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="182.37" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 182.37" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,182.37) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 182.37 L 623.38 182.37 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 182.37 L 623.38 182.37 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 6.7)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="168.97" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 168.97)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">issue<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (medium)</span></span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p3.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. The clearest appearance concern is the unusually smooth, rendered quality of the woman’s face during the close-up application sequence. Across the cheek, nose, and jaw, the skin has broad, nearly textureless tonal gradients, while the eyelashes, lip outline, ear, and nearby bottle edges remain comparatively crisp. The cheek droplets also appear as clean, rounded highlights against this uniformly softened surface. This combination gives the face a waxy, synthetic appearance rather than simply making the entire image soft. The effect persists as her hand moves across the cheek, making it more than an isolated blurred view. Confidence is medium because cosmetic smoothing and image processing can produce similar cues, and the frames do not establish a separate, unmistakable boundary failure.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 2 </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="A6.p3.pic1.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">physical_consistency[0.0--5.0 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The preceding appearance review raises a possible synthetic-rendering concern, but that concern is not by itself decisive because cosmetic smoothing, lighting, and compression can create similar visual effects. The next question is whether the depicted action obeys ordinary physical continuity. The presenter handles a bottle, raises a dropper, and brings liquid toward her face, so the full five-second interval should be checked for stable hand anatomy, plausible contact, consistent object motion, and coherent liquid behavior. A physical-consistency analysis over the same range is useful because it can either provide independent support for the appearance concern or reveal that the motion remains plausible despite visual stylization. The available one-second overview is sparse, so this check should be interpreted with appropriate caution, particularly around the exact moment of dropper contact and any brief transitions between sampled frames.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="184.53" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 184.53" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,184.53) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 184.53 L 623.38 184.53 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="171.12" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 168.97)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">issue<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (medium)</span></span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p6.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. The woman holds a dropper above an open bottle and then brings it toward her face. In the close views, the dropper tip and the small amount of liquid on her cheek are visible, but the frames do not clearly show a continuous, mechanically clear transfer from the dropper to the skin. The dropper is held upright with its tip near the bottle opening in the earlier close views, then appears separated from the bottle as she raises it; the later cheek contact is shown in a different pose. This makes the liquid’s path and the precise contact relationship difficult to follow. The woman’s hand and arm movements otherwise look broadly plausible, and the frames do not establish a definite structural deformation or impossible body motion. The concern is limited to the visible dropper-to-skin interaction, where continuity and contact are not convincingly demonstrated.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 3 </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p7.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent  <span id="A6.p3.pic1.p7.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ocr_consistency[@ 4.0 s]</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Reasoning.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p8.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> 
The two preceding full-range checks leave the media’s printed and displayed lettering as an important unresolved area. The scene contains several product packages and a large background sign, and generated imagery often produces locally unstable or malformed glyphs even when the overall composition looks coherent. A targeted OCR consistency check at 4.0 seconds is appropriate because the close-up composition makes the foreground bottle and nearby text more legible than in the opening wide view. This call should compare the apparent lettering across localized regions and determine whether any irregularity is confined to low-resolution text or affects prominent, readable labels. Such evidence is supporting rather than standalone proof: perspective, focus, motion, and stylized branding can reduce recognition quality. Nevertheless, a high-confidence text anomaly in a clear frame would materially strengthen the synthetic-media hypothesis when combined with the earlier temporal appearance and physical-continuity findings.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="184.4" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 184.4" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,184.4) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 184.4 L 623.38 184.4 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 184.4 L 623.38 184.4 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.36em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="171" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 168.84)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Sub-agent returns.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">text suspicious<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (high)</span></span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">. </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;">Issues:</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> Malformed and irregularly branching strokes in the prominent bottle label; Fused strokes and unstable character boundaries across multiple smaller label lines; Structurally unresolved lettering on both foreground and background bottles. </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;">Reason:</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p9.pic1.1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> The supplied crops show repeated glyph-structure defects across separate text regions. The prominent label provides the clearest evidence, while the smaller lines and background label show additional supporting degradation. The assessment rests on visible stroke formation, not on the OCR strings or the wording they represent.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-bg-color:#000000;"> Step 4 </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p10.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p10.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Main agent: final verdict  <span id="A6.p3.pic1.p10.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B03030;">answer(fake)</span></span></span>
</span><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_left" style="width:100%;height:0.4pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_align_left ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.p3.pic1.p11.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="189.29" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 623.38 189.29" width="623.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,189.29) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 189.29 L 623.38 189.29 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 2.77 0 L 2.77 189.29 L 623.38 189.29 L 623.38 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 8.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.92em;--ltx-fo-height:14.77em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:8.5pt;" height="175.89" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 173.73)" width="598.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p11.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.92em;">
<span id="A6.p3.pic1.p11.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p11.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Verdict.</span><span id="A6.p3.pic1.p11.pic1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> The evidence converges on a synthetic-media classification. The full-range visual inspection identifies a persistent waxy, unusually smooth facial surface with crisp nearby details, which is a medium-confidence appearance concern rather than an unmistakable boundary failure. The physical review independently finds a medium-confidence issue in the dropper-to-cheek interaction: the sampled poses do not clearly establish a continuous liquid transfer, although the broader hand and arm motion remains plausible. That limitation means the physical result is supportive, not decisive. The strongest evidence comes from the targeted text analysis at 4.0 seconds, which reports high-confidence malformed, fused, and structurally unresolved lettering across multiple foreground and background regions, including the prominent bottle label. These defects are not merely uncertain OCR readings; they concern visible glyph formation. Taken together, the repeated text irregularities, persistent rendered facial appearance, and unclear liquid contact outweigh the otherwise plausible staging and motion. The appropriate classification is fake.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span></span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
